How it works

The third footnote block lists, per municipality, what the place actually had — a district court, a tax office, a notary, schools, a deanery, a power station, a brewery, cooperatives. For a birthplace-level covariate this is the richest thing in the volume: it measures institutional presence, not demography.

It arrives in two forms in the same sentence, and the split decides what can be read from a text layer at all:

  • Abbreviations — o. hjtm., b. úř., gymn., měšť. šk., kl., elektrárna, and the single-letter cooperative codes. Plain text. This module decodes them against reference/places/institution_abbreviations.csv.
  • Pictograms — obecná škola, doctor, pharmacy, fire brigade, post. The OCR renders these as glyph noise (Щ1, gg§!, ф) and no amount of parsing recovers a symbol the engine never identified.

The pictograms are emitted anyway, as unresolved slots. The text layer still knows a marker was printed and where, so each one becomes a row with its page and position and an empty code. That makes the eventual vision pass a join — ship the crops, get codes back, fill the column — rather than a re-parse of everything. Designing it in now costs one column; retrofitting it later would mean re-running the whole extraction.

Measured 2026-08-06, and it breaks that plan: the slots are not all the markers. Over the 20-page pilot the text layer emits 291 unresolved slots where the image reads find 893 printed symbols (glm-ocr) and 545 (qwen3.5) — a threefold undercount, with only 16 of 221 municipality entries agreeing exactly and 185 holding more symbols than the ALTO saw. The cause is visible in _GLYPH_RE, which can only recognise a marker that OCR'd into something that is not a letter. A pictogram the engine rendered as Щ, ф or $ becomes a slot; the same pictogram rendered as g, f, p or S — which is the commoner outcome — is indistinguishable from type and is never emitted at all. Page 270 prints four symbols in 1, 1) [school] II, [doctor], [fire-brigade], [cooperative]: R; the ALTO gives g II, $, f, R. and yields one slot.

So "the text layer knows where every marker is, the image read knows what it is" is false, and which third it knows is decided by how the OCR happened to fail. join_symbols can still fill a slot, but its count guard cannot be a gate: the two channels are not counting the same thing, so a disagreement is the normal case and not evidence about the reader. For the offices sections the image read has to be the primary record and this module's slots a lower bound — which moves the burden of proof onto two independent readers agreeing (compare_passes) rather than onto agreement with the ALTO.

Two cautions that come from the source rather than from the code:

  • The two editions disagree on letters. A building cooperative is St in the Czech volume and B in the German. Never join the editions on the letter.
  • The language suffix is the point and it does not survive. Hč versus Hn marks a cooperative as Czech or German — an ethnic-institutional variable with no equivalent in the census — and the OCR keeps it on 2 occurrences in 188. It is recorded as language_suffix where present and left empty otherwise, never guessed.

class Abbreviation:
    code: str
    lang: str
    expansion: str
    english: str
    category: str
    kind: str
    note: str = ""

    @property
    def key(self) -> str:
        return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", self.code.strip())

def load_abbreviations(path: str | Path, lang: str='', volume: str='') -> list[Abbreviation]

Read the curated table, longest code first.

volume (a profile slug, maehren_de) reads the table's volumes column (0.11.0, D-146): blank, the row is every volume's; a slug, it is printed by the volumes named only; -slug, by every volume but that one. A German volume's plate is not the Böhmen plate: Mähren and Schlesien print a cooperative mark, a Lokalie, a Jagdhütte and more that Böhmen does not, and lack its Alpenwirtshaus. A caller that names no volume gets the rows no volume is restricted to — for German, the Böhmen set, exactly as before.

Order matters: o. hjtm. has to be tried before o., and měšť. šk. before šk., or the general code swallows the specific one and the inventory silently loses its most informative entries.

lang restricts the table to one edition's codes and is close to mandatory. The two editions do not merely translate each other, they reuse each other's letters for different things: S is sonstige Genossenschaft in the German volume and nothing at all in the Czech one, so loading both against Czech text turned stray glyph noise (S I-, S H) into 27 phantom cooperatives.

def load_abbreviations(path: str | Path, lang: str = "", volume: str = "") -> list[Abbreviation]:
    """Read the curated table, longest code first.

    ``volume`` (a profile slug, ``maehren_de``) reads the table's ``volumes`` column
    (0.11.0, D-146): blank, the row is every volume's; a slug, it is printed by the
    volumes named only; ``-slug``, by every volume but that one. A German volume's plate
    is not the Böhmen plate: Mähren and Schlesien print a cooperative mark, a Lokalie,
    a Jagdhütte and more that Böhmen does not, and lack its Alpenwirtshaus. A caller
    that names no volume gets the rows no volume is restricted to — for German, the
    Böhmen set, exactly as before.

    Order matters: ``o. hjtm.`` has to be tried before ``o.``, and ``měšť. šk.``
    before ``šk.``, or the general code swallows the specific one and the inventory
    silently loses its most informative entries.

    ``lang`` restricts the table to one edition's codes and is close to mandatory.
    The two editions do not merely translate each other, they reuse each other's
    letters for different things: ``S`` is *sonstige Genossenschaft* in the German
    volume and nothing at all in the Czech one, so loading both against Czech text
    turned stray glyph noise (``S I-``, ``S H``) into 27 phantom cooperatives.
    """
    rows: list[Abbreviation] = []
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        for row in csv.DictReader(fh):
            if not (row.get("code") or "").strip():
                continue
            if lang and (row.get("lang") or "").strip() not in (lang, ""):
                continue
            scope = (row.get("volumes") or "").split()
            only = [s for s in scope if not s.startswith("-")]
            if (only and volume not in only) or f"-{volume}" in scope:
                continue
            rows.append(Abbreviation(
                code=row["code"].strip(), lang=row.get("lang", "").strip(),
                expansion=row.get("expansion", "").strip(),
                english=row.get("english", "").strip(),
                category=row.get("category", "").strip(),
                kind=row.get("kind", "").strip(),
                note=row.get("note", "").strip()))
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda a: -len(a.key))

class Entry:
    """One municipality's institution list, as printed."""

    district: str
    page: str
    muni_seq: int
    settlement_seq: str
    text: str
    index: int
    seq_printed: str = ""
    seq_repaired: bool = False

def parse_entries(section) -> list[Entry]

Cut one offices section into per-municipality entries.

The municipality number is read, never reconstructed, and the difference matters more than it looks.

This used to force a number that fell outside a consecutive run back onto the running count, on the reasoning that entries are printed in ascending order. They are — but not consecutively. The offices section lists only the municipalities that have something to record, so the printed sequence has legitimate gaps: page 118's Jirkov prints 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15. The repair rewrote that to 1..12, and from the first gap onward every institution in the section was filed under the wrong municipality.

It could never have helped, either. _ENTRY_KEY_RE only matches when the figure is digits, so an unreadable number is not a match at all — it is folded into the entry above by _entry_chunks. Every number the repair ever saw was legible, so the repair only ever fired on a gap it mistook for damage. A fallback that cannot reach the case it was written for, and corrupts the case it does reach, is worse than none.

What is genuinely suspect is a number that goes backwards, which no printed sequence does. That is flagged in seq_repaired and left in place, because a flagged wrong number can be found later and a silently corrected one cannot.

Cut on the printed lines first. Running the key pattern over the section's joined text made the entry boundary depend on the terminal period surviving the scan, and it does not: 36% of the volume's offices entries were being swallowed by the entry above, taking their institutions with them under another municipality's number. The line break is the boundary the press set, and a key found inside a line — a second municipality printed after a full stop — still splits, so nothing that worked before stops working.

One entry per printed part (0.5.0). A municipality with several parts prints 1, 1) … — 2) … — 3) …; each — n) opens a new Entry with the same muni_seq and settlement_seq n (see _PART_CONT_RE). Before this, the continuation stayed inside the first part's text and every institution after it was filed under part 1. index still runs in printed order, so join_symbols, which orders a municipality's markers by (entry_index, position), sees exactly the sequence it saw before.

Both printed forms of that marker (0.7.0). A part that opens a new line is printed as a bare n) with no dash; _open_line_part restores the dash while the line is folded into its municipality, so it splits here too.

def parse_entries(section) -> list[Entry]:
    """Cut one offices section into per-municipality entries.

    The municipality number is **read, never reconstructed**, and the difference
    matters more than it looks.

    This used to force a number that fell outside a consecutive run back onto the
    running count, on the reasoning that entries are printed in ascending order.
    They are — but not *consecutively*. The offices section lists only the
    municipalities that have something to record, so the printed sequence has
    legitimate gaps: page 118's Jirkov prints 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14,
    15. The repair rewrote that to 1..12, and from the first gap onward every
    institution in the section was filed under the wrong municipality.

    It could never have helped, either. ``_ENTRY_KEY_RE`` only matches when the
    figure is digits, so an unreadable number is not a match at all — it is folded
    into the entry above by :func:`_entry_chunks`. Every number the repair ever saw
    was legible, so the repair only ever fired on a gap it mistook for damage. A
    fallback that cannot reach the case it was written for, and corrupts the case
    it does reach, is worse than none.

    What is genuinely suspect is a number that goes *backwards*, which no printed
    sequence does. That is flagged in ``seq_repaired`` and left in place, because a
    flagged wrong number can be found later and a silently corrected one cannot.

    **Cut on the printed lines first.** Running the key pattern over the section's
    joined text made the entry boundary depend on the terminal period surviving
    the scan, and it does not: 36% of the volume's offices entries were being
    swallowed by the entry above, taking their institutions with them under
    another municipality's number. The line break is the boundary the press set,
    and a key found *inside* a line — a second municipality printed after a full
    stop — still splits, so nothing that worked before stops working.

    **One entry per printed part** (0.5.0). A municipality with several parts prints
    ``1, 1) … — 2) … — 3) …``; each ``— n)`` opens a new :class:`Entry` with the same
    ``muni_seq`` and ``settlement_seq`` ``n`` (see :data:`_PART_CONT_RE`). Before
    this, the continuation stayed inside the first part's text and every
    institution after it was filed under part 1. ``index`` still runs in printed
    order, so :func:`join_symbols`, which orders a municipality's markers by
    ``(entry_index, position)``, sees exactly the sequence it saw before.

    **Both printed forms of that marker** (0.7.0). A part that opens a new line is
    printed as a bare ``n)`` with no dash; :func:`_open_line_part` restores the
    dash while the line is folded into its municipality, so it splits here too.
    """
    entries: list[Entry] = []
    for chunk in _entry_chunks(section):
        marks = list(_ENTRY_KEY_RE.finditer(chunk))
        for i, mark in enumerate(marks):
            end = marks[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(marks) else len(chunk)
            printed = mark.group(1)
            value = int(printed)
            # Non-monotonic is a misread digit; a *gap* is not. Flagged, never
            # overwritten — see the note above on why the old repair was pure loss.
            # Judged once per printed municipality number, before its parts are
            # appended: a continuation repeats the number by construction.
            suspect = bool(entries) and value <= entries[-1].muni_seq
            parts = _split_parts(chunk[mark.end():end],
                                 _settlement_seq(mark.group(2)))
            previous = int(parts[0][0]) if parts[0][0].isdigit() else None
            for k, (settlement, text) in enumerate(parts):
                # A part number that does not rise is the same kind of evidence as a
                # municipality number that goes backwards: usually a later key the
                # OCR destroyed, so its parts were folded in here. Over the text
                # layer of the whole volume 28 of 527 multi-part municipalities do
                # this. Flagged, never renumbered.
                backwards = (k > 0 and previous is not None
                             and int(settlement) <= previous)
                if k > 0:
                    previous = int(settlement)
                entries.append(Entry(
                    district=section.key, page=section.page,
                    muni_seq=value, settlement_seq=settlement,
                    text=text.strip(" .,;"),
                    index=len(entries), seq_printed=printed,
                    seq_repaired=(suspect and k == 0) or backwards))
    return entries

def decode_entry(entry: Entry, abbreviations: list[Abbreviation]) -> list[dict]

Everything one entry records: decoded abbreviations plus unresolved glyphs.

Matches are consumed as they are found so a long code is not re-reported by a shorter one nested inside it, and the remaining glyph runs are emitted as icon rows with an empty code for the vision pass to fill.

Consumed by blanking, not by deleting, and the difference is the join. A match used to be replaced by a single space, which shortened the string, so every offset after it moved and the glyph runs found later carried positions into a string that no longer existed. Blanking the span keeps every position true to entry.text, which is what lets the k-th unresolved marker here be identified with the k-th named symbol a vision pass returns for the same entry — see join_symbols. The records are returned in printed order for the same reason; they used to come back in abbreviation-table order, which is an artefact of the loop rather than a fact about the page.

def decode_entry(entry: Entry, abbreviations: list[Abbreviation]) -> list[dict]:
    """Everything one entry records: decoded abbreviations plus unresolved glyphs.

    Matches are consumed as they are found so a long code is not re-reported by a
    shorter one nested inside it, and the remaining glyph runs are emitted as
    ``icon`` rows with an empty ``code`` for the vision pass to fill.

    **Consumed by blanking, not by deleting, and the difference is the join.** A
    match used to be replaced by a single space, which shortened the string, so
    every offset after it moved and the glyph runs found later carried positions
    into a string that no longer existed. Blanking the span keeps every position
    true to ``entry.text``, which is what lets the k-th unresolved marker here be
    identified with the k-th named symbol a vision pass returns for the same
    entry — see :func:`join_symbols`. The records are returned in **printed
    order** for the same reason; they used to come back in abbreviation-table
    order, which is an artefact of the loop rather than a fact about the page.
    """
    remaining = entry.text
    found: list[dict] = []
    coop_letter = _coop_letter_re(abbreviations)

    for abbrev in abbreviations:
        if abbrev.kind in ("qualifier", "unit"):
            continue
        pattern = _pattern_for(abbrev)
        matches = [m for m in pattern.finditer(remaining)
                   if _is_coop_letter(abbrev) or coop_letter is None
                   or not _spells_coop_letter(m, remaining, coop_letter)]
        for match in matches:
            before = remaining[max(0, match.start() - 4):match.start()]
            count = _COUNT_RE.search(before)
            suffix = _COOP_SUFFIX_RE.match(remaining[match.start():])
            # A single letter is a cooperative only where the source puts one: in
            # the list that follows the družstvo pictogram and its colon
            # (``&■=: R; K``). Elsewhere a lone capital is glyph noise, and
            # accepting it invents institutions. Kept as low confidence rather
            # than dropped, so the judgement stays visible in the output.
            confidence = "high"
            if abbrev.kind == "cooperative" and len(abbrev.key) <= 3:
                confidence = ("high" if ":" in remaining[:match.start()]
                              else "low")
            found.append({
                "confidence": confidence,
                "check": "I10_institution", "district": entry.district,
                "page": entry.page, "muni_seq": entry.muni_seq,
                "entry_index": entry.index,
                "settlement_seq": entry.settlement_seq,
                "source": "abbrev", "code": abbrev.code,
                "expansion": abbrev.expansion, "english": abbrev.english,
                "category": abbrev.category,
                "count": int(count.group(1)) if count else 1,
                "language_suffix": (suffix.group(2) if suffix else ""),
                "position": match.start(),
                "glyph": "", "context": remaining[max(0, match.start() - 12):
                                                  match.end() + 12].strip(),
            })
        for match in matches:
            remaining = (remaining[:match.start()] + " " * (match.end() - match.start())
                         + remaining[match.end():])

    for match in _GLYPH_RE.finditer(remaining):
        found.append({
            "check": "I10_institution", "district": entry.district,
            "page": entry.page, "muni_seq": entry.muni_seq,
            "settlement_seq": entry.settlement_seq,
            "entry_index": entry.index,
            "source": "icon", "code": "", "expansion": "", "english": "",
            "category": "", "count": 1, "language_suffix": "",
            "position": match.start(),
            "confidence": "unresolved", "glyph": match.group(0),
            "context": entry.text[max(0, match.start() - 12):
                                  match.end() + 12].strip(),
        })
    return sorted(found, key=lambda r: r["position"])

def decode_sections(sections, abbreviations) -> tuple[list[dict], list[Entry]]:
    """Decode every offices section. Returns ``(records, entries)``."""
    records: list[dict] = []
    entries: list[Entry] = []
    for section in sections:
        if section.kind != "offices":
            continue
        for entry in parse_entries(section):
            entries.append(entry)
            records += decode_entry(entry, abbreviations)
    return records, entries

def join_symbols(alto_records: list[dict], vision_records: list[dict], unknown: str='[?]', count_unnamed: bool=False) -> list[dict]

Name the text layer's unresolved markers from a vision pass over the same sections. Returns one record per marker, joined or refused.

Both sides are taken in printed order within an entry, which decode_entry now guarantees. An entry the vision pass never reached is reported as only_text rather than dropped: an institution inventory that quietly omits the municipalities nobody read is the same lie as one that omits the municipalities with no post office.

count_unnamed includes the image read's own unresolved marks on the right-hand side, as markers seen but not named. Off by default and on for a transcription pass, and the distinction is not cosmetic. A dedicated OCR model asked only to transcribe renders every pictogram as one placeholder, so it names nothing and its side of the join is empty — which reported all 98 entries of the glm-ocr control as "no image read reached the entry" when it had read every one of them. That wasted the control: its whole purpose is to test whether an independent reader counts the markers in an entry the way the text layer does, which is the precondition for any naming pass, and it can answer that without naming anything.

It stays off for an annotating pass, where a leftover glyph is stray punctuation the reader emitted rather than a mark it saw, and counting those would invent disagreements.

def join_symbols(alto_records: list[dict], vision_records: list[dict],
                 unknown: str = "[?]",
                 count_unnamed: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """Name the text layer's unresolved markers from a vision pass over the same
    sections. Returns one record per marker, joined or refused.

    Both sides are taken in printed order within an entry, which
    :func:`decode_entry` now guarantees. An entry the vision pass never reached is
    reported as ``only_text`` rather than dropped: an institution inventory that
    quietly omits the municipalities nobody read is the same lie as one that omits
    the municipalities with no post office.

    ``count_unnamed`` includes the image read's *own* unresolved marks on the
    right-hand side, as markers seen but not named. Off by default and on for a
    **transcription** pass, and the distinction is not cosmetic. A dedicated OCR
    model asked only to transcribe renders every pictogram as one placeholder, so
    it names nothing and its side of the join is empty — which reported all 98
    entries of the glm-ocr control as "no image read reached the entry" when it
    had read every one of them. That wasted the control: its whole purpose is to
    test whether an independent reader *counts* the markers in an entry the way
    the text layer does, which is the precondition for any naming pass, and it can
    answer that without naming anything.

    It stays off for an annotating pass, where a leftover glyph is stray
    punctuation the reader emitted rather than a mark it saw, and counting those
    would invent disagreements.

    """
    slots: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    for record in alto_records:
        if record.get("source") == "icon":
            slots.setdefault(_entry_key(record), []).append(record)

    named: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    for record in vision_records:
        if (record.get("source") == "abbrev"
                and _SYMBOL_CODE_RE.match(str(record.get("code", "")))):
            named.setdefault(_entry_key(record), []).append(record)
        elif count_unnamed and record.get("source") == "icon":
            named.setdefault(_entry_key(record), []).append(
                {**record, "code": unknown})

    # No section-level guard here. It was needed while entries aligned by
    # position, where one extra entry offset every entry after it; a printed
    # number cannot be offset by its neighbours, so a section the two channels cut
    # differently now costs the entries that differ and nothing else.
    joined: list[dict] = []

    for key in sorted(set(slots) | set(named), key=lambda k: tuple(map(str, k))):
        page, district, muni_seq = key
        order = lambda r: (r.get("entry_index", 0), r["position"])
        left = sorted(slots.get(key, []), key=order)
        right = sorted(named.get(key, []), key=order)
        # The municipality number comes from the text layer, which is the
        # numbering the rest of the pipeline joins on. The image read's own
        # reading of it is carried beside it as evidence, never as the key.
        settlement_seq = (left or right)[0].get("settlement_seq", "")
        base = {"check": "I11_symbol_join", "page": page, "district": district,
                "muni_seq": muni_seq,
                "entry_index": (left or right)[0].get("entry_index", ""),
                "settlement_seq": settlement_seq,
                "muni_seq_image": (right[0].get("muni_seq", "") if right else ""),
                "n_text_slots": len(left), "n_named": len(right)}
        if not right:
            joined.append({**base, "verdict": "only_text", "position": "",
                           "glyph": "", "code": "", "english": "", "category": "",
                           "detail": "no vision read reached this entry"})
            continue
        if not left:
            joined.append({**base, "verdict": "only_image", "position": "",
                           "glyph": "", "code": "", "english": "", "category": "",
                           "detail": "the text layer found no marker here — the "
                                     "image read may have named something the "
                                     "engine rendered as an ordinary character"})
            continue
        if len(left) != len(right):
            joined.append({
                **base, "verdict": "count_mismatch", "position": "", "glyph": "",
                "code": "", "english": "", "category": "",
                "detail": f"{len(left)} markers in the text layer against "
                          f"{len(right)} named in the image — the k-th of one is "
                          f"not the k-th of the other, so none are joined"})
            continue
        for slot, name in zip(left, right):
            unplaced = name["code"] == unknown
            joined.append({
                **base,
                # Each marker keeps the part it was printed under (0.5.0); `base`
                # carries the municipality's first part, which is right only for
                # the rows that are about the whole municipality. The image read's
                # part is preferred: it is the channel that reads the digit cleanly.
                "settlement_seq": (name.get("settlement_seq")
                                   or slot.get("settlement_seq", "")
                                   or base["settlement_seq"]),
                "verdict": "unplaced" if unplaced else "joined",
                "position": slot["position"], "glyph": slot["glyph"],
                "code": name["code"], "english": name.get("english", ""),
                "category": name.get("category", ""),
                "count": name.get("count", 1),
                "context": slot.get("context", ""),
                "detail": "" if not unplaced else
                          "the reader saw a symbol it could not place on the list",
            })
    return joined

def lexikon_1910_join_report(joined: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for I11."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_institutions v{__version__} — I11, naming the text "
             f"layer's markers from the image", ""]
    if not joined:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  nothing to join — no vision pass over these "
                                  "sections"])
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for record in joined:
        counts[record["verdict"]] = counts.get(record["verdict"], 0) + 1
    entries = len({(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"],
                    r["settlement_seq"]) for r in joined})
    lines.append(f"  {entries} municipality entries considered")
    for verdict, label in (("joined", "marker named"),
                           ("unplaced", "symbol seen, not on the list"),
                           ("count_mismatch", "counts differ — entry refused"),

                           ("only_text", "no image read reached the entry"),
                           ("only_image", "named where the text layer saw no mark")):
        if counts.get(verdict):
            lines.append(f"    {label:38s} {counts[verdict]:5d}")

    placed = [r for r in joined if r["verdict"] == "joined"]
    if placed:
        by_cat: dict[str, int] = {}
        for record in placed:
            by_cat[record["category"]] = by_cat.get(record["category"], 0) + 1
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  named markers by category:")
        for cat, n in sorted(by_cat.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
            lines.append(f"    {cat or '(uncategorised)':16s} {n:5d}")
    slots = sum(int(r["n_text_slots"]) for r in joined
                if str(r.get("n_text_slots", "")).isdigit())
    seen = sum(int(r["n_named"]) for r in joined
               if str(r.get("n_named", "")).isdigit())
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"  markers: text layer {slots}, image read {seen}"
                 + (f"  ({seen / slots:.1f}x)" if slots else ""))
    lines.append("  A large excess on the image side is expected and is NOT a "
                 "reader error. The text")
    lines.append("  layer can only see a pictogram the OCR turned into a "
                 "non-letter; one rendered as")
    lines.append("  'g' or 'f' is invisible to it. Over the pilot it saw about a "
                 "third of what was")
    lines.append("  printed, so 'counts differ' is the normal case here and the "
                 "count cannot gate the")
    lines.append("  inventory — only two independent readers agreeing can (I12).")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def place_index(blocks_by_court) -> dict:
    """``(court, muni_seq, settlement_seq) -> the printed table row``.

    ``settlement_seq`` ``"0"`` is the municipality's own line, which is what the
    printed dash means — see :func:`_settlement_seq`. A settlement carries its own
    number, restarting at 1 inside every municipality.
    """
    from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910 as lx

    index: dict = {}
    for court, blocks in (blocks_by_court or {}).items():
        for block in blocks:
            muni, status = lx.parse_int_cell(block.municipality.get("seq"))
            if status != "ok" or muni is None:
                # Column 1 is the most damaged text on the page. An unreadable
                # municipality number means this block cannot be addressed, which
                # is reported by absence rather than by a guessed number.
                continue
            index[(court, muni, "0")] = block.municipality
            for position, row in enumerate(block.settlements, start=1):
                seq, seq_status = lx.parse_int_cell(row.get("seq"))
                # Read where legible, else fall back to the printed order, which
                # for settlements *is* the numbering — they run 1..n with no gaps
                # inside a municipality, unlike the municipalities themselves.
                index[(court, muni, str(seq if seq_status == "ok" else position))] = row
    return index

def attach_places(rows: list[dict], index: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Give every inventory row the place its entry is about.

    Adds ``place_name`` and ``place_level`` (``municipality`` / ``settlement``),
    and leaves them empty where the join fails rather than falling back to the
    municipality — an institution recorded against a settlement is a fact about
    that settlement, and quietly promoting it to the obec would move it.
    """
    for row in rows:
        key = (row.get("district", ""), row.get("muni_seq"),
               str(row.get("settlement_seq", "") or "0"))
        try:
            key = (key[0], int(key[1]), key[2])
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            row["place_name"] = ""
            row["place_level"] = ""
            continue
        found = index.get(key)
        row["place_name"] = _place_name(found) if found is not None else ""
        row["place_level"] = ("" if found is None else
                              "municipality" if key[2] == "0" else "settlement")
    return rows

             + " — I14, the place each entry is about", ""]

    named = [r for r in rows if r.get("place_name")]
    entries = {(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"]) for r in rows}
    placed = {(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"]) for r in named}
    lines.append(f"  {len(rows)} inventory rows over {len(entries)} entries")
    lines.append(f"  rows given a place name: {len(named)} "
                 f"({len(named) / len(rows):.1%})")
    lines.append(f"  entries resolved to a place: {len(placed)}/{len(entries)} "
                 f"({len(placed) / max(len(entries), 1):.1%})")
    levels: dict = {}
    for row in named:
        levels[row["place_level"]] = levels.get(row["place_level"], 0) + 1
    for level, n in sorted(levels.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
        lines.append(f"    {level:14s} {n:5d}")
    sample = [r for r in named][:6]
    if sample:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  sample:")
        for row in sample:
            lines.append(f"    {row['district'][:16]:16s} "
                         f"{row['muni_seq']}, {row.get('settlement_seq') or '0'}) "
                         f"{row['place_name'][:26]:26s} {row['code']}")
    lines.append("")

                 "number the table")
    lines.append("  could not be read at, not one whose institutions are in doubt. "
                 "It is left empty")
    lines.append("  rather than promoted to the obec, which would move a "
                 "settlement's institution.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

Every pictogram is here by definition — the text layer cannot name one — and so is anything the OCR mangled past recognition. text only the text layer has it: the image read missed a code the OCR got. def build_inventory(vision_records: list[dict],
                    alto_records: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """The offices inventory, image read primary, text layer corroborating.

    One row per (entry, code). ``source`` says which channels found it:

    ``both``   the image read it and the text layer decoded it too. For an
               ordinary abbreviation this is the corroborated case.
    ``image``  only the image read has it. Every pictogram is here by definition —
               the text layer cannot name one — and so is anything the OCR mangled
               past recognition.
    ``text``   only the text layer has it: the image read missed a code the OCR
               got. Kept, because dropping it would make the inventory worse than
               either channel alone, and flagged, because it is also where the
               image reader is weakest.

    Counts are taken from the channel that owns the row, and disagreement between
    the two on a shared code is recorded in ``count_text`` rather than resolved.
    """
    def index(records):
        out: dict[tuple, dict[str, list[dict]]] = {}
        for record in records:
            if record.get("source") not in ("abbrev", "icon"):
                continue
            entry = out.setdefault(_entry_key(record), {})
            entry.setdefault(str(record.get("code", "")), []).append(record)
        return out

    right, left = index(vision_records), index(alto_records)
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for key in sorted(set(right) | set(left), key=lambda k: tuple(map(str, k))):
        page, district, muni_seq = key
        g_codes, b_codes = right.get(key, {}), left.get(key, {})
        for code in sorted(set(g_codes) | set(b_codes)):
            in_g, in_b = code in g_codes, code in b_codes
            # An unresolved mark is not a code and cannot be corroborated by one.
            if not code:
                for record in g_codes.get(code, []):
                    rows.append(_inventory_row(record, page, district, muni_seq,
                                               "image", corroborated=False))
                continue
            source = "both" if in_g and in_b else ("image" if in_g else "text")
            owned = (g_codes if in_g else b_codes)[code]
            # ONE ROW PER PART, not per municipality (0.5.0). Grouping on the
            # municipality alone took the first record's `settlement_seq` for all
            # of them, so a fire brigade printed under parts 1 and 2 became one row
            # on part 1 — the settlement-level half of D-56. The part is the owning
            # channel's reading; corroboration stays municipality-level, because
            # the two channels disagree on the part character itself (`i` / `1`).
            by_part: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
            for record in owned:
                by_part.setdefault(str(record.get("settlement_seq", "")),
                                   []).append(record)
            for part, records in by_part.items():
                row = _inventory_row(records[0], page, district, muni_seq, source,
                                     corroborated=in_g and in_b)
                row["count"] = sum(r.get("count", 1) for r in records)
                if not in_b:
                    row["count_text"] = ""
                elif len(by_part) == 1:
                    # The common case, and exactly what 0.4.0 recorded.
                    row["count_text"] = sum(r.get("count", 1) for r in b_codes[code])
                else:
                    # Several parts: the text layer's count for *this* part where its
                    # part reading agrees, blank where it does not — never the
                    # municipality total repeated on every row.
                    same = [r for r in b_codes[code]
                            if str(r.get("settlement_seq", "")) == part]
                    row["count_text"] = (sum(r.get("count", 1) for r in same)
                                         if same else "")
                rows.append(row)
    return rows

def lexikon_1910_inventory_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for I13."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_institutions v{__version__} — I13, the offices "
             f"inventory (image read primary)", ""]
    if not rows:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  nothing read"])
    by_source: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in rows:
        by_source[row["source"]] = by_source.get(row["source"], 0) + 1
    entries = len({(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"]) for r in rows})
    lines.append(f"  {len(rows)} inventory rows over {entries} municipality "
                 f"entries")
    for source, label in (("both", "image + text layer agree"),
                          ("image", "image read only"),
                          ("text", "text layer only — the image read missed it")):
        if by_source.get(source):
            lines.append(f"    {label:44s} {by_source[source]:5d}")

    symbols = [r for r in rows if str(r["code"]).startswith("[")]
    unresolved = [r for r in rows if not r["code"]]
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"  named pictograms: {len(symbols)}   "
                 f"unresolved marks still carried: {len(unresolved)}")

    # The one accuracy figure available without a transcribed legend.
    words = [r for r in rows
             if r["code"] and not str(r["code"]).startswith("[")]
    shared = [r for r in words if r["source"] in ("both", "text")]
    agreed = [r for r in shared if r["source"] == "both"]
    if shared:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"  corroboration on codes BOTH channels can read: "
                     f"{len(agreed)}/{len(shared)} = "
                     f"{len(agreed) / len(shared):.1%}")
        lines.append("    These are the ordinary abbreviations — o. s., notář, "
                     "b. úř. — which the text")
        lines.append("    layer reads well. Two different machineries on the same "
                     "ink, so this measures")
        lines.append("    the image reader's transcription without needing a "
                     "legend, and a reader that")
        lines.append("    transcribes well is the one whose symbol names are worth "
                     "having.")

    by_cat: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in rows:
        if row["code"]:
            by_cat[row["category"]] = by_cat.get(row["category"], 0) + row["count"]
    if by_cat:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  inventory by category:")
        for cat, n in sorted(by_cat.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
            lines.append(f"    {cat or '(uncategorised)':16s} {n:5d}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def compare_inventories(passes: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]

Agreement between passes on what each entry contains, not on markers.

This is the comparison that works, and the marker-level one below is kept only for the case where positions exist. join_symbols can only surface a marker where the text layer also has a slot and the two counts match, and since the text layer holds about a third of the markers, each pass surfaces a different small subset. Over the 20-page pilot that left 57 markers and made qwen's and gemma's contributions almost disjoint — so the comparison reported no disagreements at all while the true rate was around 86%. A check that can only see where two readers overlap by construction will always report agreement, which is the worst failure available to a check whose job is to find conflict.

So this runs on the I13 inventories, which hold everything each pass read. The unit is (entry, code): did this pass claim this institution for this municipality? Positions are neither needed nor available there, which is the price — two readers that both say [school] for an entry agree here even if they attached it to different marks. That is the right trade while the naming is this unreliable: which institutions a place had is the covariate, and which glyph carried it is not.

Only entries every pass read are compared. Elsewhere a missing claim means "not read", not "disagreed", and pooling the two would score coverage as conflict.

No call site found in the notebooks or utils/ — possibly superseded or reserved for interactive use.

    municipality? Positions are neither needed nor available there, which is the
    price — two readers that both say ``[school]`` for an entry agree here even if
    they attached it to different marks. That is the right trade while the naming
    is this unreliable: which institutions a place had is the covariate, and which
    glyph carried it is not.

    Only entries **every** pass read are compared. Elsewhere a missing claim means
    "not read", not "disagreed", and pooling the two would score coverage as
    conflict.
    """
    # A pass that names nothing cannot agree or disagree about a name. Counting
    # a transcription pass among the voters makes unanimity arithmetically
    # impossible and reports 0.0% as though it were a measurement — the same shape
    # of error as a check whose denominator decides its own answer. Such a pass is
    # still read for *coverage*, so it still constrains which entries count.
    labels = sorted(lab for lab, rows in passes.items()
                    if any(str(r.get("code", "")).startswith("[") for r in rows))
    claims: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
    seen: dict[str, set] = {lab: set() for lab in passes}
    for label, rows in passes.items():
        for row in rows:
            entry = (row.get("page", ""), row.get("district", ""),
                     row.get("muni_seq"))
            seen[label].add(entry)
            code = str(row.get("code", ""))
            if not code.startswith("["):        # symbols only
                continue
            slot = claims.setdefault(entry + (code,),
                                     {"by": {}, "category": "", "english": ""})
            if label in labels:
                slot["by"][label] = int(row.get("count", 1) or 1)
            slot["category"] = row.get("category", "")
            slot["english"] = row.get("english", "")
    shared = set.intersection(*seen.values()) if seen else set()

    out: list[dict] = []
    for key in sorted(claims, key=lambda k: tuple(map(str, k))):
        page, district, muni_seq, code = key
        if (page, district, muni_seq) not in shared:
            continue
        slot = claims[key]
        record = {"check": "I12_inventory_agreement", "page": page,
                  "district": district, "muni_seq": muni_seq, "code": code,
                  "english": slot["english"], "category": slot["category"],
                  "n_claiming": len(slot["by"]), "n_passes": len(labels),
                  "verdict": ("unanimous" if len(slot["by"]) == len(labels)
                              else "contested")}
        for label in labels:
            record["count_" + label] = slot["by"].get(label, "")
        out.append(record)
    return out

def lexikon_1910_inventory_agreement_report(records, labels) -> str:
    """Ledger for the inventory-level comparison."""
    lines = ["lexikon_1910_institutions v" + __version__ + " — I12, what "
             + str(len(labels)) + " passes say each entry contains", ""]
    if not records:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  no entry was read by every pass"])
    lines.append("  naming passes: " + ", ".join(labels))
    unan = [r for r in records if r["verdict"] == "unanimous"]
    entries = len({(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"]) for r in records})
    lines.append(f"  {len(records)} (entry, symbol) claims over {entries} "
                 f"municipality entries that every pass read")
    lines.append(f"    every pass claims it   {len(unan):5d}  "
                 f"{len(unan) / len(records):5.1%}")
    lines.append(f"    only some do           {len(records) - len(unan):5d}  "
                 f"{1 - len(unan) / len(records):5.1%}")
    for label in labels:
        mine = sum(1 for r in records if r.get("count_" + label) != "")
        lines.append(f"    {label:12s} claims {mine:5d} of them")
    contested: dict[str, int] = {}
    for record in records:
        if record["verdict"] != "unanimous":
            contested[record["code"]] = contested.get(record["code"], 0) + 1
    if contested:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  most contested symbols (claimed by some passes, not all):")
        for code, n in sorted(contested.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:12]:
            lines.append(f"    {n:4d}x  {code}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("  Low unanimity here is a statement about the *naming*, not "
                 "about the readers'")
    lines.append("  eyesight: all of them transcribe the words of these entries "
                 "well. They are being")
    lines.append("  asked to map a printed 1916 glyph onto an English description "
                 "they have never")
    lines.append("  seen drawn. That is what the symbol atlas is for.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def describe_reference(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """What a reference pass covers, counted from its rows rather than typed.

    Every report that names the gold prints this, so the line cannot go on saying
    "4 pages, 280 claims" after the gold has changed underneath it.
    """
    entries, _units, claims = _claim_counts(rows, "settlement")
    _entries, _units, at_muni = _claim_counts(rows, "municipality")
    pages = sorted({str(entry[0]) for entry in entries})
    return (f"{len(pages)} pages ({', '.join(pages)}), {len(entries)} entries, "
            f"{len(claims)} claims at settlement level, {len(at_muni)} at "
            f"municipality level")

def score_against_reference(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], reference: str='human') -> list[dict]

Precision and recall of each pass against one pass taken as truth.

Two units, side by side (0.6.0, D-56). The headline is the (entry, settlement, code) claim — did this reader say this part of the municipality had this institution — in the *_settlement keys, because the settlement is what a birthplace joins to. The (entry, code) figure every earlier report used stays in the unsuffixed keys, unchanged, the same unit compare_inventories uses.

Presence ignores counts at both levels: two schools read as one is a different and much smaller error than a school read as a chapel, and pooling them would let the second hide inside the first. The printed count is scored beside it (count_exact, f1_count; see _settlement_scores).

Returns one row per pass, sorted best first on the settlement F1. entries_missed is the transcriber's entries the pass never reached — excluded from precision and recall, and reported so that a pass cannot buy accuracy by reading less.

entry_exact is the share of shared entries whose whole claim set matches the reference's. F1 pools claims across entries, so it rises when a pass moves claims around without finishing a single municipality — and a municipality is the unit of analysis downstream, where a settlement either has its institutions right or does not. A run whose F1 improves while entry_exact does not has not got closer to a usable page.

def score_against_reference(passes: dict[str, list[dict]],
                            reference: str = "human") -> list[dict]:
    """Precision and recall of each pass against one pass taken as truth.

    **Two units, side by side (0.6.0, D-56).** The headline is the
    ``(entry, settlement, code)`` claim — did this reader say this *part* of the
    municipality had this institution — in the ``*_settlement`` keys, because
    the settlement is what a birthplace joins to. The ``(entry, code)`` figure
    every earlier report used stays in the unsuffixed keys, unchanged, the same
    unit :func:`compare_inventories` uses.

    Presence ignores counts at both levels: two schools read as one is a
    different and much smaller error than a school read as a chapel, and pooling
    them would let the second hide inside the first. The printed count is scored
    beside it (``count_exact``, ``f1_count``; see :func:`_settlement_scores`).

    Returns one row per pass, sorted best first on the settlement F1.
    ``entries_missed`` is the
    transcriber's entries the pass never reached — excluded from precision and
    recall, and reported so that a pass cannot buy accuracy by reading less.

    ``entry_exact`` is the share of shared entries whose whole claim set matches
    the reference's. F1 pools claims across entries, so it rises when a pass
    moves claims around without finishing a single municipality — and a
    municipality is the unit of analysis downstream, where a settlement either
    has its institutions right or does not. A run whose F1 improves while
    ``entry_exact`` does not has not got closer to a usable page.
    """
    if reference not in passes:
        return []
    ref_entries, ref_claims = _claims(passes[reference])
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for label, records in passes.items():
        if label == reference:
            continue
        entries, claims = _claims(records)
        shared = ref_entries & entries
        mine = {c for c in claims if c[:3] in shared}
        theirs = {c for c in ref_claims if c[:3] in shared}
        hit = mine & theirs
        precision = len(hit) / len(mine) if mine else 0.0
        recall = len(hit) / len(theirs) if theirs else 0.0
        by_entry: dict[tuple, set] = {e: set() for e in shared}
        for claim in mine:
            by_entry[claim[:3]].add(claim[3])
        ref_by_entry: dict[tuple, set] = {e: set() for e in shared}
        for claim in theirs:
            ref_by_entry[claim[:3]].add(claim[3])
        exact = sum(1 for e in shared if by_entry[e] == ref_by_entry[e])
        rows.append({
            "check": "I14_accuracy", "pass": label, "reference": reference,
            "entries_shared": len(shared),
            "entries_missed": len(ref_entries - entries),
            "reference_claims": len(theirs), "claims": len(mine),
            "hit": len(hit), "false": len(mine - theirs),
            "missed": len(theirs - mine),
            "entries_exact": exact,
            "entry_exact": round(exact / len(shared), 3) if shared else 0.0,
            "precision": round(precision, 3), "recall": round(recall, 3),
            "f1": round(2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall), 3)
                  if precision + recall else 0.0,
            **_settlement_scores(passes[reference], records),
        })
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (-r["f1_settlement"], -r["f1"], r["pass"]))

    lines.append("  comparison only; ent.ex (whole entry exactly right) is no "
                 "longer a headline.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def symbol_confusion(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], label: str,
                     reference: str = "human") -> list[dict]:
    """Per-symbol counts, one pass against the reference, on entries both read.

    An F1 is a summary and hides its own shape. Whether a reader is uniformly
    blurry or is missing two specific glyphs decides what to do next, and only
    this shows which: a symbol the reference claims 41 times and the reader
    claims 9 is one pictogram to settle, not a model to replace.
    """
    if reference not in passes or label not in passes:
        return []
    ref_entries, ref_claims = _claims(passes[reference])
    entries, claims = _claims(passes[label])
    shared = ref_entries & entries
    english = {}
    for records in (passes[reference], passes[label]):
        for row in records:
            code = str(row.get("code", "") or "")
            if code.startswith("[") and row.get("english"):
                english.setdefault(code, row["english"])
    codes = {c[3] for c in ref_claims | claims if c[:3] in shared}
    rows = []
    for code in codes:
        in_ref = sum(1 for c in ref_claims if c[:3] in shared and c[3] == code)
        in_pass = sum(1 for c in claims if c[:3] in shared and c[3] == code)
        rows.append({"check": "I15_symbol_error", "pass": label,
                     "reference": reference, "code": code,
                     "english": english.get(code, ""),
                     "reference_claims": in_ref, "pass_claims": in_pass,
                     "delta": in_pass - in_ref})
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (-abs(r["delta"]),
                                       -r["reference_claims"]))

    """Ledger for :func:`symbol_confusion` — the glyphs worth a human's time."""
    if not rows:
        return "  nothing to compare"
    lines = [f"  {rows[0]['pass']} vs {rows[0]['reference']}, symbol by symbol "
             f"(entries both read)", ""]
    lines.append(f"  {'symbol':20s} {'reference':>9s} {'pass':>6s} "
                 f"{'delta':>6s}")
    for row in rows[:top]:
        lines.append(f"  {row['code']:20s} {row['reference_claims']:9d} "
                     f"{row['pass_claims']:6d} {row['delta']:+6d}")
    agreed = [r for r in rows if r["delta"] == 0]
    if agreed:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"  exact on {len(agreed)} of {len(rows)} symbols: "
                     + ", ".join(r["code"] for r in agreed[:8])
                     + ("…" if len(agreed) > 8 else ""))
    return "\n".join(lines)

def symbol_rates(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], label: str, reference: str='human', level: str='settlement', units: set | None=None) -> list[dict]

Sensitivity and specificity of one pass, glyph by glyph.

For each symbol, every unit on the entries both sides read is one of tp (both claim it), fp (only the pass), fn (only the reference) or tn (neither). sensitivity = tp / (tp + fn) and specificity = tn / (tn + fp); either is blank, not zero, where its denominator is empty — a glyph the reference never prints has no measured sensitivity.

units is the universe of units, as entry + (part,) tuples (or bare entries at municipality level). Left out, it is every unit either inventory has a row for — and an inventory only has rows where something was printed or read, so a part with no institutions at all is missing from it. Those are true negatives for every glyph, so the default understates specificity; pass the parts read from the gold sheets to close that.

def symbol_rates(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], label: str,
                 reference: str = "human", level: str = "settlement",
                 units: set | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Sensitivity and specificity of one pass, glyph by glyph.

    For each symbol, every unit on the entries both sides read is one of
    ``tp`` (both claim it), ``fp`` (only the pass), ``fn`` (only the reference)
    or ``tn`` (neither). ``sensitivity = tp / (tp + fn)`` and
    ``specificity = tn / (tn + fp)``; either is **blank**, not zero, where its
    denominator is empty — a glyph the reference never prints has no measured
    sensitivity.

    ``units`` is the universe of units, as ``entry + (part,)`` tuples (or bare
    entries at ``municipality`` level). Left out, it is every unit either
    inventory has a row for — and an inventory only has rows where something
    was printed or read, so a part with no institutions at all is missing from
    it. Those are true negatives for every glyph, so the default **understates
    specificity**; pass the parts read from the gold sheets to close that.
    """
    if reference not in passes or label not in passes:
        return []
    _shared, seen, theirs, mine = _shared_claims(passes[reference],
                                                 passes[label], level)
    shared_entries = {c[:3] for c in seen}
    universe = {c[:-1] for c in theirs.keys() | mine.keys()}
    universe |= ({u for u in units if u[:3] in shared_entries}
                 if units is not None else seen)
    rows = []
    for code in sorted({c[-1] for c in theirs.keys() | mine.keys()}):
        in_ref = {c for c in theirs if c[-1] == code}
        in_pass = {c for c in mine if c[-1] == code}
        tp, fp, fn = (len(in_ref & in_pass), len(in_pass - in_ref),
                      len(in_ref - in_pass))
        tn = len(universe) - tp - fp - fn
        rows.append({"check": "I16_symbol_rates", "pass": label,
                     "reference": reference, "level": level, "code": code,
                     "units": len(universe), "tp": tp, "fp": fp, "fn": fn,
                     "tn": tn,
                     "sensitivity": round(tp / (tp + fn), 3) if tp + fn else "",
                     "specificity": round(tn / (tn + fp), 3) if tn + fp else ""})
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (-(r["fp"] + r["fn"]), r["code"]))

def part_attribution(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], label: str,
                     reference: str = "human") -> list[dict]:
    """Institutions the pass names correctly and files under the wrong part.

    One row per ``(entry, code)`` that both sides claim for the municipality but
    on different parts. This is the whole of the gap between the municipality
    and settlement figures, itemised: the decoder's ``— n)`` continuation was
    its largest term (fixed in 0.5.0), and what is left has not been diagnosed.
    ``kind`` sorts the rows so the residue can be read as a pattern rather than
    a list — see :func:`_misfiling_kind`.
    """
    if reference not in passes or label not in passes:
        return []
    _shared, _units, theirs, mine = _shared_claims(passes[reference],
                                                   passes[label], "settlement")

    def parts(claims) -> dict[tuple, set]:
        out: dict[tuple, set] = {}
        for claim in claims:
            out.setdefault(claim[:3] + (claim[-1],), set()).add(claim[3])
        return out

    ref_parts, my_parts = parts(theirs), parts(mine)
    rows = []
    for key in sorted(ref_parts.keys() & my_parts.keys(),
                      key=lambda k: tuple(map(str, k))):
        want, got = ref_parts[key], my_parts[key]
        if want == got:
            continue
        page, district, muni_seq, code = key
        rows.append({"check": "I17_part_attribution", "pass": label,
                     "reference": reference, "page": page,
                     "district": district, "muni_seq": muni_seq, "code": code,
                     "reference_parts": " ".join(sorted(want)),
                     "pass_parts": " ".join(sorted(got)),
                     "kind": _misfiling_kind(want, got)})
    return rows

def lexikon_1910_part_attribution_report(rows: list[dict], top: int = 10) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`part_attribution`."""
    if not rows:
        return "  every institution both sides name is filed under the same parts"
    lines = [f"  {rows[0]['pass']} vs {rows[0]['reference']}: {len(rows)} "
             f"institutions named correctly and filed under the wrong part", ""]

    def tally(key) -> list[tuple]:
        counts: dict = {}
        for row in rows:
            counts[key(row)] = counts.get(key(row), 0) + 1
        return sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], str(kv[0])))

    for title, key in (
            ("by kind", lambda r: r["kind"]),
            ("by page", lambda r: r["page"]),
            ("by parts, reference -> pass",
             lambda r: f"{r['reference_parts']} -> {r['pass_parts']}"),
            ("by symbol", lambda r: r["code"])):
        lines.append(f"  {title}:")
        for value, n in tally(key)[:top]:
            lines.append(f"    {n:4d}x  {value}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def clustered_interval(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], label: str,
                       reference: str = "human", level: str = "settlement",
                       draws: int = 2000,
                       seed: int = BOOTSTRAP_SEED) -> dict:
    """F1 with a percentile interval from resampling **pages**, not claims.

    Claims on one page share a scan, a print run, a district and the crops the
    reader was shown, so they are one cluster and not that many independent
    draws. Each bootstrap draw picks pages with replacement and pools their hit
    / false / missed counts into one F1.

    ``f1_by_page`` is printed beside the interval because with few pages it is
    the more honest object: ``G`` pages allow few distinct resamples, so the
    percentile interval is coarse and too narrow. ``f1_lo`` and ``f1_hi`` are
    blank with fewer than two pages.
    """
    blank = {"check": "I18_clustered_interval", "pass": label,
             "reference": reference, "level": level, "pages": 0, "draws": draws,
             "f1": "", "f1_lo": "", "f1_hi": "", "f1_by_page": ""}
    if reference not in passes or label not in passes:
        return blank
    _shared, _units, theirs, mine = _shared_claims(passes[reference],
                                                   passes[label], level)
    counts: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
    for claim in theirs.keys() | mine.keys():
        slot = counts.setdefault(str(claim[0]), [0, 0, 0])
        slot[0 if claim in theirs and claim in mine
             else 1 if claim in mine else 2] += 1
    if not counts:
        return blank
    pages = sorted(counts)
    pooled = lambda picked: _prf(*(sum(counts[p][k] for p in picked)
                                   for k in range(3)))[2]
    out = {**blank, "pages": len(pages), "f1": round(pooled(pages), 3),
           "f1_by_page": " ".join(f"{p}={pooled([p]):.3f}" for p in pages)}
    if len(pages) < 2 or draws < 1:
        return out
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    f1s = sorted(pooled([rng.choice(pages) for _ in pages])
                 for _ in range(draws))
    out["f1_lo"] = round(f1s[int(_TAIL * draws)], 3)
    out["f1_hi"] = round(f1s[max(int((1 - _TAIL) * draws) - 1, 0)], 3)
    return out

def second_reader(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], first: str, second: str, reference: str='human', level: str='settlement') -> dict

Which of the first reader's errors a second reader would bring to review.

A claim both readers make, or neither does, is accepted; a claim only one of them makes is flagged. So the second reader's own accuracy is not the figure that matters — where its errors fall is:

caught errors of the first the second disagrees with it on. They reach review. shared_errors errors both make. Nothing in the pair shows them, and they are what is left in the data after a perfect review. false_alarms claims the first has right and the second does not: review load that buys nothing.

f1_after_review is the first reader's F1 if every flagged claim were settled correctly — the ceiling this pair can reach, not a forecast.

The missed_* block is the test D-58 asks for. Given the truth, two readers' errors should fall independently; on the claims the reference has, the number both miss is then hypergeometric and missed_p is its upper tail (Fisher's exact test, one-sided — the exact form of the permutation check). A small missed_p says the two miss the same claims more often than chance would have it: a shared blind spot. Two cautions. Claims on one page are not independent draws, so the tail is too small rather than too large; and with a dozen misses the test has little power, so a large missed_p is not evidence of independence. False claims get no such test — it needs the universe of claims that could have been made — and are counts.

Scored on the entries all three read, at level; presence only.

def second_reader(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], first: str, second: str,
                  reference: str = "human", level: str = "settlement") -> dict:
    """Which of the first reader's errors a second reader would bring to review.

    A claim both readers make, or neither does, is accepted; a claim only one of
    them makes is flagged. So the second reader's own accuracy is not the figure
    that matters — where its errors fall is:

    ``caught``        errors of the first the second disagrees with it on. They
                      reach review.
    ``shared_errors`` errors both make. Nothing in the pair shows them, and they
                      are what is left in the data after a perfect review.
    ``false_alarms``  claims the first has right and the second does not: review
                      load that buys nothing.

    ``f1_after_review`` is the first reader's F1 if every flagged claim were
    settled correctly — the ceiling this pair can reach, not a forecast.

    The ``missed_*`` block is the test D-58 asks for. Given the truth, two
    readers' errors should fall independently; on the claims the reference has,
    the number both miss is then hypergeometric and ``missed_p`` is its upper
    tail (Fisher's exact test, one-sided — the exact form of the permutation
    check). A small ``missed_p`` says the two miss the same claims more often
    than chance would have it: a shared blind spot. **Two cautions.** Claims on
    one page are not independent draws, so the tail is too small rather than too
    large; and with a dozen misses the test has little power, so a large
    ``missed_p`` is not evidence of independence. False claims get no such test —
    it needs the universe of claims that could have been made — and are counts.

    Scored on the entries all three read, at ``level``; presence only.
    """
    blank = {"check": "I21_second_reader", "first": first, "second": second,
             "reference": reference, "level": level, "entries_shared": 0}
    if not all(name in passes for name in (reference, first, second)):
        return blank
    read = [_claim_counts(passes[name], level)
            for name in (reference, first, second)]
    shared = read[0][0] & read[1][0] & read[2][0]
    truth, one, two = ({c for c in claims if c[:3] in shared}
                       for _entries, _units, claims in read)
    errors_one, errors_two, flagged = one ^ truth, two ^ truth, one ^ two
    missed_one, missed_two = truth - one, truth - two
    false_both, missed_both = (one - truth) & (two - truth), missed_one & missed_two
    share = lambda n, d: round(n / d, 3) if d else ""           # noqa: E731
    return {
        **blank, "entries_shared": len(shared), "reference_claims": len(truth),
        "first_errors": len(errors_one), "second_errors": len(errors_two),
        "caught": len(errors_one & flagged),
        "shared_errors": len(errors_one & errors_two),
        "catch_rate": share(len(errors_one & flagged), len(errors_one)),
        "flagged": len(flagged), "false_alarms": len(flagged - errors_one),
        "f1_first": round(_prf(len(one & truth), len(one - truth),
                               len(missed_one))[2], 3),
        "f1_after_review": round(_prf(len(truth) - len(missed_both),
                                      len(false_both), len(missed_both))[2], 3),
        "missed_first": len(missed_one), "missed_second": len(missed_two),
        "missed_both": len(missed_both),
        "missed_both_expected": (round(len(missed_one) * len(missed_two)
                                       / len(truth), 2) if truth else ""),
        "missed_p": round(_excess_tail(len(truth), len(missed_one),
                                       len(missed_two), len(missed_both)), 4),
        "false_first": len(one - truth), "false_second": len(two - truth),
        "false_both": len(false_both),
    }

def lexikon_1910_second_reader_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`second_reader`, one line per pair of readers."""
    rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("entries_shared")]
    if not rows:
        return "  nothing to compare"
    lines = [f"  what a second reader would bring to review — "
             f"{rows[0]['level']} level, against {rows[0]['reference']}", "",
             f"  {'first':22s} {'second':22s} {'errors':>6s} {'caught':>6s} "
             f"{'rate':>6s} {'shared':>6s} {'alarms':>6s} {'F1':>6s} {'F1 after':>8s}"]
    for row in rows:
        rate = f"{row['catch_rate']:.3f}" if row["catch_rate"] != "" else "—"
        lines.append(
            f"  {row['first']:22s} {row['second']:22s} {row['first_errors']:6d} "
            f"{row['caught']:6d} {rate:>6s} {row['shared_errors']:6d} "
            f"{row['false_alarms']:6d} {row['f1_first']:6.3f} "
            f"{row['f1_after_review']:8.3f}")
    lines += ["", "  claims the reference has that both readers miss — observed, "
                  "expected if their", "  misses fell independently, and the chance "
                  "of that many or more (D-58):", ""]
    for row in rows:
        chance = (f"p = {row['missed_p']:.4f}" if row["missed_p"] >= 0.0001
                  else "p < 0.0001")
        lines.append(
            f"  {row['first']:22s} {row['second']:22s} "
            f"{row['missed_first']:3d} and {row['missed_second']:3d} of "
            f"{row['reference_claims']}: both {row['missed_both']:3d}, expected "
            f"{row['missed_both_expected']}, {chance}   "
            f"false: {row['false_first']} and {row['false_second']}, "
            f"both {row['false_both']}")
    lines += ["", "  `caught` reaches review; `shared` is what a perfect review "
                  "still leaves; `alarms`",
              "  is review load on claims the first reader had right. A small p "
              "is a shared blind",
              "  spot. A large one is not independence: with this few misses "
              "the test is weak."]
    return "\n".join(lines)

def order_runs(records: list[dict], text: str | None=None) -> list[list[dict]]

One entry's symbol records, in printed order, cut where the order restarts.

records are decode_entry's for one entry — one numbered part, which is where the order restarts anyway. They are sorted by position and cut again at each named part (Valdice:). Returns the runs, each a list of the records themselves; runs with no symbol are left out.

With the entry's text the cut is _ORDER_NAMED_PART_RE and a mark inside parentheses is dropped. Without it — a pass stored as institutions_&lt;label&gt;.csv keeps the records and not the text — the cut is read off each record's context.

Blind to, without the text: a named part whose first words are not a mark (Kartouzy: věznice …, [doctor]), because the name is then outside the mark's window; and parentheses, so a mark the reader wrote inside them is judged with the rest.

def order_runs(records: list[dict], text: str | None = None) -> list[list[dict]]:
    """One entry's symbol records, in printed order, cut where the order restarts.

    ``records`` are :func:`decode_entry`'s for **one** entry — one numbered part,
    which is where the order restarts anyway. They are sorted by ``position``
    and cut again at each named part (``Valdice:``). Returns the runs, each a
    list of the records themselves; runs with no symbol are left out.

    With the entry's ``text`` the cut is :data:`_ORDER_NAMED_PART_RE` and a mark
    inside parentheses is dropped. Without it — a pass stored as
    ``institutions_<label>.csv`` keeps the records and not the text — the cut is
    read off each record's ``context``.

    **Blind to, without the text:** a named part whose first words are not a
    mark (``Kartouzy: věznice …, [doctor]``), because the name is then outside
    the mark's window; and parentheses, so a mark the reader wrote inside them
    is judged with the rest.
    """
    marks = sorted((r for r in records if _order_code(r)),
                   key=lambda r: int(r.get("position") or 0))
    if text is None:
        runs: list[list[dict]] = []
        for record in marks:
            context = str(record.get("context", "") or "")
            before = context[:max(context.find(record["code"]), 0)]
            if not runs or _ORDER_NAMED_BEFORE_RE.search(before):
                runs.append([])
            runs[-1].append(record)
        return runs
    spans = [m.span() for m in _ORDER_PAREN_RE.finditer(text)]
    blanked = _ORDER_PAREN_RE.sub(lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), text)
    cuts = [m.end() for m in _ORDER_NAMED_PART_RE.finditer(blanked)]
    by_part: dict[int, list[dict]] = {}
    for record in marks:
        position = int(record.get("position") or 0)
        if any(start <= position < end for start, end in spans):
            continue
        by_part.setdefault(sum(1 for cut in cuts if cut <= position),
                           []).append(record)
    return [by_part[part] for part in sorted(by_part)]

reference is one row per run, {"page": …, "codes": [...]}, as read_transcription_md.read_order_reference returns it. Every pair of positions holding two different marks counts once, adjacent or not.

leave_out_page drops one page's runs. Use it when the result will judge a reading of that same page: the page's own gold would otherwise vouch for whatever order the reader copied off it, right or wrong.

Blind to: anything about a pair the reference never prints together — it is absent from the result, and absent is "not judged", never "allowed".

def learn_order(reference: list[dict], leave_out_page: str = "") -> dict:
    """``{(a, b): n}`` — how often the reference prints mark ``a`` before ``b``.

    ``reference`` is one row per run, ``{"page": …, "codes": [...]}``, as
    ``read_transcription_md.read_order_reference`` returns it. Every pair of
    positions holding two different marks counts once, adjacent or not.

    ``leave_out_page`` drops one page's runs. Use it when the result will judge
    a reading of that same page: the page's own gold would otherwise vouch for
    whatever order the reader copied off it, right or wrong.

    **Blind to:** anything about a pair the reference never prints together —
    it is absent from the result, and absent is "not judged", never "allowed".
    """
    before: dict[tuple, int] = {}
    for row in reference:
        if leave_out_page and str(row.get("page", "")) == str(leave_out_page):
            continue
        codes = row["codes"]
        for i in range(len(codes)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(codes)):
                if codes[i] != codes[j]:
                    pair = (codes[i], codes[j])
                    before[pair] = before.get(pair, 0) + 1
    return before

def out_of_order(codes: list[str], order: dict, min_seen: int=ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> list[int]

Positions of the fewest marks whose removal leaves no reversed pair.

codes is one run's marks in printed order (order_runs), order is learn_order's. A castle read as a poorhouse at the end of a line stands after the post, the telegraph and the station, all of which the print sets after a poorhouse — several reversed pairs, one mark in all of them, and that mark is the answer. Empty when nothing is reversed.

Blind to:

  • a same-slot substitution — station for stop, revenue office for customs, one church for another, a savings bank written straight before the cooperative. The wrong mark stands where the right one would, so no pair is reversed. Most of what the readers still get wrong is this;
  • which of two — one reversed pair between two marks says one of them is wrong, not which. The later one is returned; the caller shows both;
  • a missing mark, which reverses nothing;
  • the three marks of ORDER_FLOATING, wherever they stand;
  • a pair the reference shows fewer than min_seen times. The reference is ten pages of one edition, the Czech one.

    ``codes`` is one run's marks in printed order (:func:`order_runs`),

    of a line stands after the post, the telegraph and the station, all of
    which the print sets after a poorhouse — several reversed pairs, one mark
    in all of them, and that mark is the answer. Empty when nothing is reversed.

    **Blind to:**

    * a **same-slot substitution** — station for stop, revenue office for
      customs, one church for another, a savings bank written straight before
      the cooperative. The wrong mark stands where the right one would, so no
      pair is reversed. Most of what the readers still get wrong is this;
    * **which of two** — one reversed pair between two marks says one of them is
      wrong, not which. The later one is returned; the caller shows both;
    * a **missing** mark, which reverses nothing;
    * the three marks of :data:`ORDER_FLOATING`, wherever they stand;
    * a pair the reference shows fewer than ``min_seen`` times. The reference is
      ten pages of one edition, the Czech one.
    """
    return _smallest_cover(_reversed_pairs(codes, order, min_seen))

def order_restart(codes: list[str], order: dict, min_seen: int=ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> int | None

Where the order begins again inside one run, or None.

The second verdict. If every reversed pair runs across one point — the marks before it in order among themselves, the marks from it on in order among themselves, and only the two groups out of order with each other — the marks are not misread, the run is two: a part or an entry boundary was missed (— 2) lost, two printed lines joined, a named part's colon dropped). That is a parsing question, and it is reported as one.

Returns the position of the first mark of the second group, which is the first mark that belongs before something printed earlier. A mark between the two groups that is reversed with nothing could sit on either side.

Blind to: a second part too short to show — ORDER_RESTART_MIN marks must be out of place, so a one-mark part run on from below, or one whose only reversed mark is its first, comes back from out_of_order as that mark; a second part that only repeats marks of the first ([school] … — 2) [school]), because a mark is never reversed with itself; and the reverse error — two neighbouring marks both misread as marks that belong earlier (the gendarme and canteen after a fire brigade read as [customs], [gauging]) divide the line the same way and are called a restart too.
