def order_restart(codes: list[str], order: dict,
                  min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> int | None:
    """Where the order begins again inside one run, or ``None``.

    The second verdict. If every reversed pair runs across one point — the marks
    before it in order among themselves, the marks from it on in order among
    themselves, and only the two groups out of order with each other — the
    marks are not misread, the run is two: a part or an entry boundary was
    missed (``— 2)`` lost, two printed lines joined, a named part's colon
    dropped). That is a **parsing question**, and it is reported as one.

    Returns the position of the first mark of the second group, which is the
    first mark that belongs before something printed earlier. A mark between
    the two groups that is reversed with nothing could sit on either side.

    **Blind to:** a second part too short to show —
    :data:`ORDER_RESTART_MIN` marks must be out of place, so a one-mark part run
    on from below, or one whose only reversed mark is its first, comes back from
    :func:`out_of_order` as that mark; a second part that only repeats marks
    of the first (``[school] … — 2) [school]``), because a mark is never
    reversed with itself; and the reverse error — two neighbouring marks both
    misread as marks that belong earlier (the gendarme and canteen after a fire
    brigade read as ``[customs]``, ``[gauging]``) divide the line the same way
    and are called a restart too.
    """
    pairs = _reversed_pairs(codes, order, min_seen)
    if not pairs:
        return None
    cut = min(j for _i, j in pairs)
    if max(i for i, _j in pairs) >= cut:
        return None
    return cut if len(_smallest_cover(pairs)) >= ORDER_RESTART_MIN else None

def check_order(records: list[dict], reference: list[dict], texts: dict | None=None, leave_page_out: bool=False, min_seen: int=ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> list[dict]

verdict is VERDICT_OUT_OF_PLACE (look at this mark) or VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS (look at where this part was cut; the rows are then the marks out_of_order names, and restart_code is the first mark of the second group). against lists the marks each one is reversed with, sequence the whole run as read.

def check_order(records: list[dict], reference: list[dict],
                texts: dict | None = None, leave_page_out: bool = False,
                min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> list[dict]:
    """One row per mark the printed order sends to review. Changes no record.

    ``records`` are decoded records of any number of entries
    (:func:`decode_sections`, or a stored ``institutions_<label>.csv``);
    ``reference`` is what :func:`learn_order` takes. ``texts`` maps
    ``(page, district, entry_index)`` to the entry's text where the caller has
    it. ``leave_page_out`` learns the order afresh for each page from the other
    pages — required when the records are readings of the reference's own
    pages, which is the case whenever this is scored.

    ``verdict`` is :data:`VERDICT_OUT_OF_PLACE` (look at this mark) or
    :data:`VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS` (look at where this part was cut; the rows
    are then the marks :func:`out_of_order` names, and ``restart_code`` is the
    first mark of the second group). ``against`` lists the marks each one is
    reversed with, ``sequence`` the whole run as read.
    """
    by_entry: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    for record in records:
        by_entry.setdefault(_order_entry(record), []).append(record)
    orders: dict[str, dict] = {}
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for entry, mine in by_entry.items():
        page = entry[0] if leave_page_out else ""
        if page not in orders:
            orders[page] = learn_order(reference, leave_out_page=page)
        text = (texts or {}).get((entry[0], entry[1], entry[4]))
        for named_part, run in enumerate(order_runs(mine, text)):
            codes = [record["code"] for record in run]
            pairs = _reversed_pairs(codes, orders[page], min_seen)
            if not pairs:
                continue
            restart = order_restart(codes, orders[page], min_seen)
            for position in _smallest_cover(pairs):
                against = [codes[j if i == position else i]
                           for i, j in pairs if position in (i, j)]
                rows.append({
                    "check": "I22_order", "page": entry[0], "district": entry[1],
                    "muni_seq": entry[2], "settlement_seq": entry[3],
                    "entry_index": entry[4], "named_part": named_part,
                    "code": codes[position],
                    "position": run[position].get("position", ""),
                    "verdict": (VERDICT_OUT_OF_PLACE if restart is None
                                else VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS),
                    "against": " ".join(dict.fromkeys(against)),
                    "restart_code": "" if restart is None else codes[restart],
                    "sequence": " ".join(codes)})
    return rows

def order_summary(reference: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """What the reference order rests on, counted from its rows rather than typed.

    ``against_majority`` counts pair observations that run the less common way
    for their pair; ``*_fixed`` is the same with :data:`ORDER_FLOATING` left
    out, and is the figure the check stands on.
    """
    order = learn_order(reference)
    pairs = {tuple(sorted(pair)) for pair in order}
    fixed = [p for p in pairs if not set(p) & ORDER_FLOATING]
    seen = lambda p: (order.get(p, 0), order.get(p[::-1], 0))   # noqa: E731
    count = lambda some: sum(sum(seen(p)) for p in some)        # noqa: E731
    minority = lambda some: sum(min(seen(p)) for p in some)     # noqa: E731
    return {"pages": len({str(row.get("page", "")) for row in reference}),
            "runs": len(reference),
            "marks": sum(len(row["codes"]) for row in reference),
            "pairs": len(pairs), "observations": count(pairs),
            "against_majority": minority(pairs),
            "pairs_fixed": len(fixed), "observations_fixed": count(fixed),
            "against_majority_fixed": minority(fixed)}

def order_reference_flags(reference: list[dict],
                          min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> list[dict]:
    """The reference's own runs that the other pages' order would flag.

    Each page is judged on the order learned without it. A row here is a line
    of a gold sheet to look at again — a slip of the transcriber's, or a place
    where the print departs from its own order. It is reported and nothing is
    changed: the sheets are the author's to rule on.
    """
    rows = []
    for run in reference:
        order = learn_order(reference, leave_out_page=run.get("page", ""))
        codes = run["codes"]
        marks = out_of_order(codes, order, min_seen)
        if marks:
            restart = order_restart(codes, order, min_seen)
            rows.append({**{k: v for k, v in run.items() if k != "codes"},
                         "verdict": (VERDICT_OUT_OF_PLACE if restart is None
                                     else VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS),
                         "marks": " ".join(codes[i] for i in marks),
                         "sequence": " ".join(codes)})
    return rows

def order_joins(reference: list[dict], min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> dict:
    """Would the order have shown a missed boundary? Simulated on the reference.

    Each two runs printed one after the other in the same municipality — two
    numbered parts, or two named parts of one — are run together, as a decoder
    that missed the boundary would leave them, and judged on the order learned
    without their page. ``shown`` is how many joins leave any mark out of place;
    ``restarts`` how many of those get the parsing verdict of
    :func:`order_restart`. ``one_mark`` counts the joins whose shorter side is a
    single mark, which can never be called a restart.

    A power check on the check, not a property of any reader.
    """
    out = {"joins": 0, "shown": 0, "restarts": 0, "one_mark": 0}
    municipality = lambda row: (row.get("page"), row.get("district"),   # noqa: E731
                                row.get("muni_seq"))
    for above, below in zip(reference, reference[1:]):
        if municipality(above) != municipality(below):
            continue
        order = learn_order(reference, leave_out_page=above.get("page", ""))
        joined = above["codes"] + below["codes"]
        out["joins"] += 1
        out["one_mark"] += min(len(above["codes"]), len(below["codes"])) == 1
        out["shown"] += bool(out_of_order(joined, order, min_seen))
        out["restarts"] += order_restart(joined, order, min_seen) is not None
    return out

def order_scores(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], flags: dict[str, list[dict]],
                 reference: str = "human", level: str = "settlement",
                 sheets: list[dict] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """What the order check flags in each pass, against the reference's truth.

    ``passes`` are inventories, the reference among them; ``flags`` maps a
    label to its :func:`check_order` rows. Scored as the accuracy table is: on
    the entries the pass and the reference both read, at ``level``, presence
    only. A claim is flagged when any mark carrying it is.

    ``false_flagged`` is the check doing its work; ``true_flagged`` is review
    load on claims that were right. ``restart_parts`` counts the parts given
    the parsing verdict, on any page.

    ``flagged_elsewhere`` counts flagged claims on entries the reference does
    not cover. With ``sheets`` — the order reference's own runs — those are
    held against the sheet's line for the part: ``elsewhere_on_sheets`` are on
    a part some sheet transcribes, ``elsewhere_absent`` are marks that sheet
    does not print there. **These two are weaker evidence than the scored
    columns:** the sheets outside the scored gold are single-coded and partly
    still drafts, and they are the sheets the order was learned from (each
    page is judged on the others, so no line vouches for itself).
    """
    sheet_units, sheet_claims = set(), {}
    if sheets:
        _entries, sheet_units, sheet_claims = _claim_counts(
            order_sheet_rows(sheets), level)
    rows = []
    for label, records in passes.items():
        if label == reference or label not in flags:
            continue
        shared, _units, theirs, mine = _shared_claims(passes[reference], records,
                                                      level)
        flagged = set(_claim_counts(flags[label], level)[2])
        false, true = mine.keys() - theirs.keys(), mine.keys() & theirs.keys()
        elsewhere = {c for c in flagged if c[:3] not in shared}
        on_sheets = {c for c in elsewhere if c[:-1] in sheet_units}
        rows.append({
            "check": "I22_order", "pass": label, "reference": reference,
            "level": level, "false": len(false),
            "false_flagged": len(false & flagged), "true": len(true),
            "true_flagged": len(true & flagged),
            "flagged_elsewhere": len(elsewhere),
            "elsewhere_on_sheets": len(on_sheets),
            "elsewhere_absent": len(on_sheets - sheet_claims.keys()),
            "restart_parts": len({_order_entry(row) + (row["named_part"],)
                                  for row in flags[label]
                                  if row["verdict"] == VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS})})
    return rows

def order_disputes(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], flags: dict[str, list[dict]], first: str, second: str, reference: str='human', level: str='settlement') -> dict

What the order says about the claims two readers disagree on.

A disputed claim is one only one of the two makes, on the entries both and the reference read — the claims second_reader sends to review. The order check can speak on such a claim only through the reader that made it: flagged counts the disputed claims whose maker's reading it flags, flagged_false those of them the reference does not have (the flag points at the wrong side of the dispute, correctly), flagged_true those it does (the flag is wrong). The first_* and second_* keys split the same counts by who made the claim.

agreed_false are the false claims both make — accepted by the pair unseen, since nothing is disputed — and agreed_false_flagged those of them a mark out of place carries in either reading. The order does not depend on the two readers disagreeing, so it can reach these.

It routes: a flag is a reason to look at that reader's mark first, and settles nothing by itself.

Blind to: a disputed claim that is missing from one reader. Its absence reverses no pair, so the check is silent on the reader that dropped it and can only ever speak against the one that wrote it.

def order_disputes(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], flags: dict[str, list[dict]],
                   first: str, second: str, reference: str = "human",
                   level: str = "settlement") -> dict:
    """What the order says about the claims two readers disagree on.

    A disputed claim is one only one of the two makes, on the entries both and
    the reference read — the claims :func:`second_reader` sends to review. The
    order check can speak on such a claim only through the reader that made
    it: ``flagged`` counts the disputed claims whose maker's reading it flags,
    ``flagged_false`` those of them the reference does not have (the flag
    points at the wrong side of the dispute, correctly), ``flagged_true`` those
    it does (the flag is wrong). The ``first_*`` and ``second_*`` keys split
    the same counts by who made the claim.

    ``agreed_false`` are the false claims **both** make — accepted by the pair
    unseen, since nothing is disputed — and ``agreed_false_flagged`` those of
    them a mark out of place carries in either reading. The order does not
    depend on the two readers disagreeing, so it can reach these.

    It routes: a flag is a reason to look at that reader's mark first, and
    settles nothing by itself.

    **Blind to:** a disputed claim that is *missing* from one reader. Its
    absence reverses no pair, so the check is silent on the reader that
    dropped it and can only ever speak against the one that wrote it.
    """
    blank = {"check": "I22_order", "first": first, "second": second,
             "reference": reference, "level": level, "disputed": 0}
    names = (reference, first, second)
    if not all(name in passes for name in names) or not all(
            name in flags for name in (first, second)):
        return blank
    read = [_claim_counts(passes[name], level) for name in names]
    shared = read[0][0] & read[1][0] & read[2][0]
    truth, one, two = ({c for c in claims if c[:3] in shared}
                       for _entries, _units, claims in read)
    marked = {name: set(_claim_counts(flags[name], level)[2])
              for name in (first, second)}
    agreed_false = (one & two) - truth
    out = {**blank, "disputed": len(one ^ two),
           "disputed_false": len((one ^ two) - truth),
           "agreed_false": len(agreed_false),
           "agreed_false_flagged": len(agreed_false
                                       & (marked[first] | marked[second]))}
    total = {"flagged": 0, "flagged_false": 0, "flagged_true": 0}
    for who, made, name in (("first", one - two, first),
                            ("second", two - one, second)):
        flagged = made & marked[name]
        mine = {"flagged": len(flagged), "flagged_false": len(flagged - truth),
                "flagged_true": len(flagged & truth)}
        out.update({f"{who}_disputed": len(made),
                    f"{who}_disputed_false": len(made - truth),
                    **{f"{who}_{key}": n for key, n in mine.items()}})
        total = {key: total[key] + n for key, n in mine.items()}
    return {**out, **total}

def lexikon_1910_order_report(summary: dict, scores: list[dict],
                              sheet_flags: list[dict] | None = None,
                              joins: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """Ledger for I22: the reference, then each pass (:func:`order_scores`)."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_institutions v{__version__} — I22, the printed order "
             f"of the marks", "",
             f"  reference order: {summary['runs']} runs of marks on "
             f"{summary['pages']} gold pages, {summary['marks']} symbols, "
             f"{summary['pairs']} pairs seen together",
             f"  pair observations {summary['observations']}, "
             f"{summary['against_majority']} against the majority direction; "
             f"without {', '.join(sorted(ORDER_FLOATING))}:",
             f"  {summary['observations_fixed']} observations of "
             f"{summary['pairs_fixed']} pairs, "
             f"{summary['against_majority_fixed']} against the majority"]
    if joins:
        lines += ["", f"  two adjacent parts run together, simulated on the "
                      f"reference: {joins['shown']} of {joins['joins']} joins "
                      f"leave a mark out of place,",
                  f"  {joins['restarts']} of them called a restart; in "
                  f"{joins['one_mark']} joins the shorter part is one mark, "
                  f"which is never called one"]
    if sheet_flags is not None:
        ruling = (" — for the author's eye, nothing is changed"
                  if sheet_flags else "")
        lines += ["", f"  gold lines the other pages' order flags: "
                      f"{len(sheet_flags)}{ruling}"]
        lines += [f"    {row.get('page', '')} {row.get('district', '')} "
                  f"{row.get('muni_seq', '')},{row.get('settlement_seq', '')}  "
                  f"{row['verdict']}: {row['marks']}   in: {row['sequence']}"
                  for row in sheet_flags]
    if not scores:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["", "  no pass with stored records to judge"])
    lines += ["", f"  each pass, order learned leaving the judged page out, a "
                  f"pair counted from {ORDER_MIN_SEEN} sightings — "
                  f"{scores[0]['level']} level", "",
              f"  {'':26s} {'— scored gold —':^26s}   "
              f"{'— other pages —':^26s}",
              f"  {'pass':26s} {'false':>5s} {'flagged':>7s} {'true':>5s} "
              f"{'flagged':>7s}   {'flagged':>7s} {'on sheet':>8s} "
              f"{'absent':>6s} {'restarts':>9s}"]
    for row in scores:
        lines.append(f"  {row['pass']:26s} {row['false']:5d} "
                     f"{row['false_flagged']:7d} {row['true']:5d} "
                     f"{row['true_flagged']:7d}   {row['flagged_elsewhere']:7d} "
                     f"{row['elsewhere_on_sheets']:8d} "
                     f"{row['elsewhere_absent']:6d} {row['restart_parts']:9d}")
    lines += ["", "  false / true = the pass's claims the reference does not / "
                  "does have; flagged = of those,",
              "  the ones a mark out of place carries. other pages = flagged "
              "claims outside the scored",
              "  gold; on sheet = of those, on a part a calibration sheet "
              "transcribes; absent = the",
              "  sheet does not print that mark there (single-coded sheets, "
              "some still drafts: weaker",
              "  evidence than the scored columns). restarts = parts, on any "
              "page, where the order",
              "  begins again: a boundary to check, not a symbol. The check "
              "flags and routes; no claim",
              "  is changed by it.",
              "  It cannot see a mark misread as another of the same slot "
              "(station / stop,",
              "  revenue office / customs, a savings bank before the "
              "cooperative), nor a missing mark."]
    return "\n".join(lines)

def lexikon_1910_order_disputes_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`order_disputes`, one line per pair of readers.

    ``rows`` may be single pairs of passes or means over the repeats of two
    readers; the columns are the same and are printed to one decimal.
    """
    rows = [row for row in rows if row.get("disputed")]
    if not rows:
        return "  no pair of passes with stored records to compare"
    lines = [f"  the order check on disputed claims — {rows[0]['level']} level, "
             f"against {rows[0]['reference']}", "",
             f"  {'first':22s} {'second':22s} {'disputed':>8s} {'false':>6s} "
             f"{'flagged':>7s} {'right':>6s} {'wrong':>6s} {'on 1st':>7s} "
             f"{'on 2nd':>7s}   {'agreed false':>12s} {'flagged':>7s}"]
    for row in rows:
        lines.append(f"  {row['first']:22s} {row['second']:22s} "
                     f"{row['disputed']:8.1f} {row['disputed_false']:6.1f} "
                     f"{row['flagged']:7.1f} {row['flagged_false']:6.1f} "
                     f"{row['flagged_true']:6.1f} {row['first_flagged']:7.1f} "
                     f"{row['second_flagged']:7.1f}   {row['agreed_false']:12.1f} "
                     f"{row['agreed_false_flagged']:7.1f}")
    lines += ["", "  disputed = claims only one of the two makes; false = of "
                  "those, not in the reference.",
              "  flagged = disputed claims whose maker's mark is out of place; "
              "right = the claim is",
              "  indeed false; wrong = it is true; on 1st / on 2nd = whose "
              "claim the flag is on.",
              "  A flag says which reading to look at first, and settles "
              "nothing by itself.",
              "  agreed false = false claims both make, which the pair accepts "
              "unseen; flagged = of",
              "  those, the ones a mark out of place carries in either "
              "reading."]
    return "\n".join(lines)

def compare_passes(passes: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
    """Per-marker agreement across two or more symbol passes.

    ``passes`` maps a label (``"qwen"``, ``"gemma"``) to that run's
    :func:`join_symbols` output. Returns one record per *marker*, carrying each
    pass's answer in its own ``code_<label>`` column so the CSV can be read
    without a join.

    Verdicts, and why each is separate:

    ``unanimous``  every pass named it, and named it the same. The strongest thing
                   available without a transcribed legend.
    ``split``      two or more passes named it differently. Exactly one of them is
                   right, at most — this is the adjudication worklist.
    ``partial``    the passes that named it agree, but not every pass reached it.
                   Coverage differs; the reading does not.
    ``unplaced``   nobody could place it. An honest gap, and a candidate for a
                   symbol the curated list is missing.
    """
    labels = sorted(passes)
    markers: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
    for label, records in passes.items():
        for record in records:
            if record.get("position") in ("", None):
                continue        # not addressed to a single marker
            # Keyed on the entry's position in its section, which every pass
            # derives from the same deterministic cut, plus the marker's position
            # in the entry. The printed municipality number is carried in the
            # output but is not the key: it is the text layer's reading in one
            # pass and could be a different pass's reading in another.
            key = (record.get("page", ""), record.get("district", ""),
                   record.get("entry_index"), int(record["position"]))
            slot = markers.setdefault(key, {"glyph": record.get("glyph", ""),
                                            "context": record.get("context", ""),
                                            "muni_seq": record.get("muni_seq", ""),
                                            "codes": {}})
            slot["codes"][label] = str(record.get("code", ""))

    out: list[dict] = []
    for key in sorted(markers, key=lambda k: tuple(map(str, k))):
        page, district, entry_index, position = key
        slot = markers[key]
        named = {lab: code for lab, code in slot["codes"].items()
                 if code and code != UNPLACED}
        distinct = set(named.values())
        if not named:
            verdict = "unplaced"
        elif len(distinct) > 1:
            verdict = "split"
        elif len(named) == len(labels):
            verdict = "unanimous"
        else:
            verdict = "partial"
        record = {"check": "I12_symbol_agreement", "page": page,
                  "district": district, "muni_seq": slot["muni_seq"],
                  "entry_index": entry_index, "position": position,
                  "glyph": slot["glyph"], "verdict": verdict,
                  "n_readers": len(slot["codes"]), "n_named": len(named),
                  "codes": " | ".join(sorted(distinct)),
                  "context": slot["context"]}
        for label in labels:
            record[f"code_{label}"] = slot["codes"].get(label, "")
        out.append(record)
    return out

def disagreements(records: list[dict], labels: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """The split markers, grouped by *which* two names were confused.

    Sorted by how often the confusion happens, because a pair that recurs 40 times
    is one glyph the readers systematically differ on and is worth a human looking
    at the plate once; a pair that happens once is worth looking at the scan.
    """
    groups: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    for record in records:
        if record["verdict"] != "split":
            continue
        shape = tuple(sorted({record[f"code_{lab}"] for lab in labels
                              if record.get(f"code_{lab}")}))
        groups.setdefault(shape, []).append(record)
    out: list[dict] = []
    for shape, rows in sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):
        sample = rows[0]
        out.append({"check": "I12_disagreement", "codes": " vs ".join(shape),
                    "n": len(rows), "example_page": sample["page"],
                    "example_district": sample["district"],
                    "example_muni_seq": sample["muni_seq"],
                    "example_position": sample["position"],
                    "example_glyph": sample["glyph"],
                    "example_context": sample["context"]})
    return out

def lexikon_1910_agreement_report(records: list[dict], labels: list[str]) -> str:
    """Ledger for I12."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_institutions v{__version__} — I12, the same marker "
             f"read by {len(labels)} passes", ""]
    if not records:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  no marker was addressed by any pass"])
    lines.append("  naming passes: " + ", ".join(labels))
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for record in records:
        counts[record["verdict"]] = counts.get(record["verdict"], 0) + 1
    total = len(records)
    lines.append(f"  markers addressed: {total}")
    for verdict, label in (("unanimous", "every pass named it, and agreed"),
                           ("split", "passes named it differently"),
                           ("partial", "agreed, but not every pass reached it"),
                           ("unplaced", "no pass could place it")):
        if counts.get(verdict):
            lines.append(f"    {label:42s} {counts[verdict]:5d}  "
                         f"{counts[verdict] / total:5.1%}")

    decided = counts.get("unanimous", 0) + counts.get("split", 0)
    if decided:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"  agreement where every pass named the marker: "
                     f"{counts.get('unanimous', 0)}/{decided} "
                     f"= {counts.get('unanimous', 0) / decided:.1%}")

    lines.append("")
    lines.append("  per pass:")
    for label in labels:
        named = sum(1 for r in records
                    if r.get(f"code_{label}") not in ("", UNPLACED))
        unplaced = sum(1 for r in records if r.get(f"code_{label}") == UNPLACED)
        absent = sum(1 for r in records if not r.get(f"code_{label}"))
        lines.append(f"    {label:12s} named {named:5d}   "
                     f"{UNPLACED} {unplaced:5d}   never reached {absent:5d}")

    splits = disagreements(records, labels)
    if splits:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  what they disagree about, most frequent first:")
        for row in splits[:15]:
            lines.append(f"    {row['n']:4d}x  {row['codes']}")
            lines.append(f"           e.g. p.{row['example_page']} "
                         f"{row['example_district']} muni {row['example_muni_seq']}"
                         f"  {row['example_context'][:46]!r}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("  Agreement here is weaker evidence than elsewhere in this "
                 "pipeline: both readers")
    lines.append("  choose from the same closed list, so a glyph that resembles "
                 "the wrong token")
    lines.append("  resembles it for both. Treat the split list as a worklist for "
                 "the printed legend,")
    lines.append("  not the unanimous count as an accuracy figure.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def lexikon_1910_institutions_report(records, entries, abbreviations) -> str:
    """Ledger for the institution inventory."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_institutions v{__version__} — "
             f"Úřady, ústavy (institution inventory)", ""]
    if not entries:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  no offices entries parsed"])

    decoded = [r for r in records if r["source"] == "abbrev"]
    icons = [r for r in records if r["source"] == "icon"]
    lines.append(f"  {len(entries)} municipality entries over "
                 f"{len({e.district for e in entries})} soudní okresy")
    lines.append(f"  abbreviation table: {len(abbreviations)} codes")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"  decoded from text : {len(decoded):5d}")
    lines.append(f"  unresolved icons  : {len(icons):5d}  "
                 f"({len({r['glyph'] for r in icons})} distinct glyphs) "
                 f"— emitted as slots for a vision pass")
    if decoded:
        share = len(decoded) / (len(decoded) + len(icons))
        lines.append(f"  share of markers readable as text: {share:.1%}")

    by_cat: dict[str, int] = {}
    for r in decoded:
        by_cat[r["category"]] = by_cat.get(r["category"], 0) + r["count"]
    if by_cat:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  institutions by category (counts include printed multipliers):")
        for cat, n in sorted(by_cat.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
            lines.append(f"    {cat:16s} {n:5d}")

    low = [r for r in decoded if r.get("confidence") == "low"]
    if low:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"  low-confidence single-letter matches: {len(low)} "
                     f"(no družstvo colon in the entry — likely glyph noise)")

    coops = [r for r in decoded if r["category"] == "cooperative"]
    if coops:
        with_suffix = [r for r in coops if r["language_suffix"]]
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"  cooperatives: {len(coops)}, of which "
                     f"{len(with_suffix)} carry a legible č/n language suffix "
                     f"({len(with_suffix) / len(coops):.0%})")
        lines.append("    the suffix is the ethnic marker and the OCR loses it — "
                     "this is a vision target,")
        lines.append("    not a parsing problem. Never inferred from the "
                     "surrounding language.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""Decode the ``Úřady, ústavy`` footnote into an institution inventory.

The third footnote block lists, per municipality, what the place actually had — a
district court, a tax office, a notary, schools, a deanery, a power station, a
brewery, cooperatives. For a birthplace-level covariate this is the richest thing
in the volume: it measures *institutional presence*, not demography.

It arrives in two forms in the same sentence, and the split decides what can be
read from a text layer at all:

* **Abbreviations** — ``o. hjtm.``, ``b. úř.``, ``gymn.``, ``měšť. šk.``, ``kl.``,
  ``elektrárna``, and the single-letter cooperative codes. Plain text. This module
  decodes them against ``reference/places/institution_abbreviations.csv``.
* **Pictograms** — obecná škola, doctor, pharmacy, fire brigade, post. The OCR
  renders these as glyph noise (``Щ1``, ``gg§!``, ``ф``) and no amount of parsing
  recovers a symbol the engine never identified.

**The pictograms are emitted anyway, as unresolved slots.** The text layer still
knows a marker was printed and where, so each one becomes a row with its page and
position and an empty ``code``. That makes the eventual vision pass a *join* — ship
the crops, get codes back, fill the column — rather than a re-parse of everything.
Designing it in now costs one column; retrofitting it later would mean re-running
the whole extraction.

**Measured 2026-08-06, and it breaks that plan: the slots are not all the
markers.** Over the 20-page pilot the text layer emits **291** unresolved slots
where the image reads find **893** printed symbols (glm-ocr) and **545** (qwen3.5)
— a threefold undercount, with only 16 of 221 municipality entries agreeing
exactly and 185 holding more symbols than the ALTO saw. The cause is visible in
:data:`_GLYPH_RE`, which can only recognise a marker that OCR'd into something
that is *not* a letter. A pictogram the engine rendered as ``Щ``, ``ф`` or ``$``
becomes a slot; the same pictogram rendered as ``g``, ``f``, ``p`` or ``S`` — which
is the commoner outcome — is indistinguishable from type and is never emitted at
all. Page 270 prints four symbols in ``1, 1) [school] II, [doctor], [fire-brigade],
[cooperative]: R``; the ALTO gives ``g II, $, f, R.`` and yields **one** slot.

So "the text layer knows where every marker is, the image read knows what it is"
is false, and which third it knows is decided by how the OCR happened to fail.
:func:`join_symbols` can still fill a slot, but its count guard cannot be a gate:
the two channels are not counting the same thing, so a disagreement is the normal
case and not evidence about the reader. For the offices sections the image read
has to be the *primary* record and this module's slots a lower bound — which moves
the burden of proof onto two independent readers agreeing (:func:`compare_passes`)
rather than onto agreement with the ALTO.

Two cautions that come from the source rather than from the code:

* **The two editions disagree on letters.** A building cooperative is ``St`` in the
  Czech volume and ``B`` in the German. Never join the editions on the letter.
* **The language suffix is the point and it does not survive.** ``Hč`` versus
  ``Hn`` marks a cooperative as Czech or German — an ethnic-institutional variable
  with no equivalent in the census — and the OCR keeps it on 2 occurrences in 188.
  It is recorded as ``language_suffix`` where present and left empty otherwise,
  never guessed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import math
import random
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

__version__ = "0.11.0"

#: Entries are keyed by the municipality's sequence number, then optionally a
#: settlement's: ``11, 2) …``, ``3, —) …``. The numbers are as damaged as anywhere
#: else in column 1, so they are read where legible and reconstructed by order
#: where not — see :func:`parse_entries`.
_ENTRY_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|(?<=[.;]))\s*(\d{1,3})\s*,\s*([^)]{0,3})\)")

#: A municipality's **second and later parts**: ``1, 1) … — 2) … — 3) …``. The
#: register prints the municipality number once and opens each further part with a
#: dash and the part's own number, so this is a key without its municipality.
#: :data:`_ENTRY_KEY_RE` cannot see it, and until 0.5.0 nothing split on it: every
#: institution printed after ``— 2)`` was filed under the *first* part — 35 of 273
#: correctly read claims (12.8 %) in the first E1 Gemini pass, all shifted towards
#: part 1 (D-56).
#:
#: Fitted to the text layer of the whole volume (2026-09-22): 733 continuations on
#: 454 pages, the dash read as ``-`` 420 times, ``—`` 297 and ``_`` 16, and preceded
#: by ``. `` or ``- ``. The dash must **not** follow a letter or digit, which is what
#: keeps the house–population pair (``217—2266``) and a hyphenated place name
#: (``Záluží-Ledenice``) from ever splitting an entry. The part number must be
#: digits: a continuation whose number the OCR destroyed stays folded into the part
#: above, which is where 0.4.0 put *every* continuation — no worse than before.
_PART_CONT_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\w)[—–\-−‐―~_]\s*(\d{1,2})\s*\)")

#: The same continuation where the part opens a **new printed line**. There the
#: register sets no dash at all — the bare ``2)`` hangs under the ``1)`` of the
#: line above::
#:
#:     13,  1) [school] I, [fire-brigade].
#:          2) [customs] II, [revenue-guard], 3 [gendarme], …
#:
#: (scan 0118, soudní okres Jirkov, read off the image 2026-10-05). The dash is
#: only printed when a part runs on inside a line, which is the one form
#: :data:`_PART_CONT_RE` was fitted to. Until 0.7.0 the bare line was folded into
#: the part above it. That is what misfiled Jirkov 13, Trutnov 23 and Trutnov 29,
#: the three entries holding 207 of the 211 misfiled institutions in the twelve E1
#: Gemini passes as they stood on 2026-10-05 — the "undiagnosed ~0.05" between the
#: municipality and settlement figures. Replayed from the crop caches the same
#: day: the default reader's settlement F1 went 0.915 -> 0.961 on the gold of the
#: time and met its municipality figure (D-64).
#:
#: Anchored at the start of a line, never searched for inside one: mid-line, a
#: number and a bracket is too easily something else.
#:
#: Up to two specks may stand before the number. Scan 0118 has a spot of ink
#: just left of Jirkov 13's ``2)`` and one Gemini pass transcribed it, as
#: ``°2)``; the marker is no less a marker for the dirt beside it. The set is
#: the speck-shaped characters only — never a dash, which is the other printed
#: form and already splits, and never a letter or a bracket.
_LINE_PART_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*[°˚º•·.,'‘’`]{0,2}\s*(\d{1,2})\s*\)")

#: What a part number must exceed when the part above it cannot be read: the
#: entry key's own part is at least the first, so a line can only open the second
#: or a later one.
_UNREAD_PART_FLOOR = 1

#: A count printed before an institution: ``2 adv.``, ``7 Å``, ``5 🏫 XLII``.
_COUNT_RE = re.compile(r"(\d{1,2})\s*$")

#: The language marker appended to a cooperative letter (``Hč``, ``Kn``): Czech
#: ``č``/``n`` (český, německý). The German editions write ``b``/``d`` (böhmisch,
#: deutsch), and the Mähren and Schlesien legends add ``p``, polnisch — "z. B. Kd =
#: Deutscher Konsumverein" (0.11.0, D-146). The marker is optional ("die etwa
#: hinzugefügte Abkürzung"): a bare letter states no language and keeps none.
_COOP_SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(r"^(Sch|St|[HJKPRBGLS])\s*([čcnbdp])\b")
#: The suffix as it is set hard against its letter (``Rd``, ``Schb.``, ``Rč``, ``Kp``).
_COOP_SUFFIXES = "čcnbdp"

#: A printed marker the OCR could not identify: anything that is not a Latin
#: letter, digit, space or ordinary punctuation. These are the pictograms.
_GLYPH_RE = re.compile(r"[^\w\s.,;:()\[\]/\-—–'\"§+&%]", re.UNICODE)


@dataclass
class Abbreviation:
    code: str
    lang: str
    expansion: str
    english: str
    category: str
    kind: str
    note: str = ""

    @property
    def key(self) -> str:
        return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", self.code.strip())


def load_abbreviations(path: str | Path, lang: str = "", volume: str = "") -> list[Abbreviation]:
    """Read the curated table, longest code first.

    ``volume`` (a profile slug, ``maehren_de``) reads the table's ``volumes`` column
    (0.11.0, D-146): blank, the row is every volume's; a slug, it is printed by the
    volumes named only; ``-slug``, by every volume but that one. A German volume's plate
    is not the Böhmen plate: Mähren and Schlesien print a cooperative mark, a Lokalie,
    a Jagdhütte and more that Böhmen does not, and lack its Alpenwirtshaus. A caller
    that names no volume gets the rows no volume is restricted to — for German, the
    Böhmen set, exactly as before.

    Order matters: ``o. hjtm.`` has to be tried before ``o.``, and ``měšť. šk.``
    before ``šk.``, or the general code swallows the specific one and the inventory
    silently loses its most informative entries.

    ``lang`` restricts the table to one edition's codes and is close to mandatory.
    The two editions do not merely translate each other, they reuse each other's
    letters for different things: ``S`` is *sonstige Genossenschaft* in the German
    volume and nothing at all in the Czech one, so loading both against Czech text
    turned stray glyph noise (``S I-``, ``S H``) into 27 phantom cooperatives.
    """
    rows: list[Abbreviation] = []
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        for row in csv.DictReader(fh):
            if not (row.get("code") or "").strip():
                continue
            if lang and (row.get("lang") or "").strip() not in (lang, ""):
                continue
            scope = (row.get("volumes") or "").split()
            only = [s for s in scope if not s.startswith("-")]
            if (only and volume not in only) or f"-{volume}" in scope:
                continue
            rows.append(Abbreviation(
                code=row["code"].strip(), lang=row.get("lang", "").strip(),
                expansion=row.get("expansion", "").strip(),
                english=row.get("english", "").strip(),
                category=row.get("category", "").strip(),
                kind=row.get("kind", "").strip(),
                note=row.get("note", "").strip()))
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda a: -len(a.key))


def _pattern_for(abbrev: Abbreviation) -> re.Pattern:
    """Match one code as a whole token.

    The periods inside a code are literal and the spacing around them is not
    trustworthy, so ``o. hjtm.`` also matches ``o.hjtm.`` and ``o . hjtm .``. A
    single-letter cooperative code is anchored hard on both sides — an unanchored
    ``K`` matches inside every second word.

    **A symbol token carries its own delimiters and must not be boundary-anchored.**
    ``[school]`` cannot begin inside a word the way ``o.`` can, and the letter
    boundary is what a vision reader breaks: asked to put the token where the
    symbol was printed, it writes ``o[fire-brigade]`` or ``2 měst[rc-parish]`` when
    the print set the picture hard against a word. With the boundary required, the
    decoder saw nothing there, so a symbol the reader *did* name was dropped as
    silently as one it never read — and the join then refused the whole entry for
    a count that differed by one.

    **A cooperative letter may carry its language suffix set hard against it**
    (``Rd``, ``Schb.``, ``Rč``; 0.10.0). The hard right anchor refused every one of
    them, so a suffixed cooperative was no cooperative at all. **A "suffix form"
    row** (``sch.``, ``bhf.``) is the tail of a longer word, which a word-start
    match cannot see; at a word start it is itself only as the whole word, else
    ``sch.`` decoded ``Schulrat`` and ``Schlachth.`` as schools.
    """
    if abbrev.key.startswith("[") and abbrev.key.endswith("]"):
        return re.compile(re.escape(abbrev.key), re.IGNORECASE)
    body = r"\s*\.?\s*".join(re.escape(p) for p in abbrev.key.replace(".", " ").split())
    if _is_coop_letter(abbrev):
        return re.compile(rf"(?<![^\W\d_]){body}[{_COOP_SUFFIXES}]?(?![^\W\d_])")
    if abbrev.note.startswith("suffix form"):
        return re.compile(rf"(?<![^\W\d_]){body}(?![^\W\d_])", re.IGNORECASE)
    return re.compile(rf"(?<![^\W\d_]){body}", re.IGNORECASE)


def _is_coop_letter(abbrev: Abbreviation) -> bool:
    return len(abbrev.key) <= 3 and abbrev.kind == "cooperative"


def _coop_letter_re(abbreviations: list[Abbreviation]) -> re.Pattern | None:
    """A cooperative letter exactly as printed — its capital, an optional suffix — as a
    whole word. A word code that matches only that is refused it (0.10.0): the German
    ``sch.`` (Schule) is case-blind and took every ``Sch`` credit union on the gold, and
    ``GB.`` and ``S. D.`` would take ``Gb`` and ``Sd`` the same way."""
    keys = sorted((a.key for a in abbreviations if _is_coop_letter(a)), key=len, reverse=True)
    if not keys:
        return None
    return re.compile(rf"(?:{'|'.join(map(re.escape, keys))})[{_COOP_SUFFIXES}]?")


@dataclass
class Entry:
    """One municipality's institution list, as printed."""

    district: str
    page: str
    muni_seq: int
    settlement_seq: str
    text: str
    index: int
    seq_printed: str = ""
    seq_repaired: bool = False


#: The printed dash in a settlement position, and what the OCR makes of it. A
#: register dash is not a missing value.
_DASH_RE = re.compile(r"^[\s\-‐-―−_~]+$")


def _settlement_seq(printed: str) -> str:
    """The settlement number in an entry key. A printed dash is **0**, not blank.

    ``22, —)`` means municipality 22 taken as a whole — the register writes the
    dash where there is no *separate* settlement to point at, which is a zero and
    not an absence. Rendering it as an empty string made it indistinguishable from
    the case that really is unknown: a settlement figure the scan destroyed. 875 of
    the volume's ~1,560 offices entries carry the dash, so the two were pooled on
    more than half the inventory.

    Anything non-empty that is not a dash is returned as printed, damage included
    (``i``, ``l``, ``_`` for ``1``), because a wrong character that is visible can
    be repaired later and one normalised away cannot.
    """
    raw = (printed or "").strip()
    if not raw:
        return ""
    return "0" if _DASH_RE.match(raw) else raw.strip(" ")


def _split_parts(text: str, head: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """``(settlement_seq, text)`` for each part printed in one municipality's entry.

    ``head`` is the part the entry key named (``1`` in ``1, 1)``, ``0`` for a dash).
    The text up to the first ``— n)`` belongs to it; each continuation opens the
    next part. An entry with no continuation comes back as one part, unchanged.
    """
    cuts = list(_PART_CONT_RE.finditer(text))
    parts = [(head, text[:cuts[0].start()] if cuts else text)]
    for k, cut in enumerate(cuts):
        stop = cuts[k + 1].start() if k + 1 < len(cuts) else len(text)
        parts.append((cut.group(1), text[cut.end():stop]))
    return parts


def _entry_chunks(section) -> list[str]:
    """The section's printed entries, one string each.

    Two rules composed, because neither alone is enough. The **line break** opens
    an entry, which is what the print does; but a chunk that carries no
    municipality key — a settlement continuation ``— 2)``, or an opening figure
    the OCR destroyed (``в, -)``, ``Г) o``) — is folded back into the entry above
    it, because it belongs to that municipality and dropping it would delete
    institutions rather than merely misfile them.
    """
    from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910_notes as lxnt

    chunks: list[str] = []
    for chunk in lxnt.entry_chunks(section.lines):
        if chunks and not _ENTRY_KEY_RE.search(chunk):
            chunks[-1] += " " + _open_line_part(chunks[-1], chunk)
        else:
            chunks.append(chunk)
    return chunks


def _last_part(text: str) -> int | None:
    """The part number an entry's text currently ends in, or None if unreadable."""
    keys = list(_ENTRY_KEY_RE.finditer(text))
    if not keys:
        return None
    part = _settlement_seq(keys[-1].group(2))
    for cut in _PART_CONT_RE.finditer(text, keys[-1].end()):
        part = cut.group(1)
    return int(part) if part.isdigit() else None


def _open_line_part(above: str, chunk: str) -> str:
    """Give a part that opens its own printed line the dash the print leaves out.

    ``chunk`` is a printed line with no municipality key, about to be folded into
    the entry ``above``. If it opens with a bare part number (see
    :data:`_LINE_PART_RE`) it comes back as ``— n) …``, the form
    :func:`_split_parts` already cuts on, so the two printed forms of one marker
    reach the splitter as one.

    The number must **rise** above the part the entry currently ends in. Parts are
    printed in ascending order, so a line-opening number that does not rise is not
    a part of this municipality — most often the key of the next one with its
    municipality figure lost — and it is folded in unmarked, exactly as before.
    """
    mark = _LINE_PART_RE.match(chunk)
    if not mark:
        return chunk
    last = _last_part(above)
    floor = _UNREAD_PART_FLOOR if last is None else last
    if int(mark.group(1)) <= floor:
        return chunk
    # Rewritten from the number, not prefixed: a speck left before it would
    # stand between the dash and the number and hide the marker again.
    return f"— {mark.group(1)}){chunk[mark.end():]}"


def parse_entries(section) -> list[Entry]:
    """Cut one offices section into per-municipality entries.

    The municipality number is **read, never reconstructed**, and the difference
    matters more than it looks.

    This used to force a number that fell outside a consecutive run back onto the
    running count, on the reasoning that entries are printed in ascending order.
    They are — but not *consecutively*. The offices section lists only the
    municipalities that have something to record, so the printed sequence has
    legitimate gaps: page 118's Jirkov prints 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14,
    15. The repair rewrote that to 1..12, and from the first gap onward every
    institution in the section was filed under the wrong municipality.

    It could never have helped, either. ``_ENTRY_KEY_RE`` only matches when the
    figure is digits, so an unreadable number is not a match at all — it is folded
    into the entry above by :func:`_entry_chunks`. Every number the repair ever saw
    was legible, so the repair only ever fired on a gap it mistook for damage. A
    fallback that cannot reach the case it was written for, and corrupts the case
    it does reach, is worse than none.

    What is genuinely suspect is a number that goes *backwards*, which no printed
    sequence does. That is flagged in ``seq_repaired`` and left in place, because a
    flagged wrong number can be found later and a silently corrected one cannot.

    **Cut on the printed lines first.** Running the key pattern over the section's
    joined text made the entry boundary depend on the terminal period surviving
    the scan, and it does not: 36% of the volume's offices entries were being
    swallowed by the entry above, taking their institutions with them under
    another municipality's number. The line break is the boundary the press set,
    and a key found *inside* a line — a second municipality printed after a full
    stop — still splits, so nothing that worked before stops working.

    **One entry per printed part** (0.5.0). A municipality with several parts prints
    ``1, 1) … — 2) … — 3) …``; each ``— n)`` opens a new :class:`Entry` with the same
    ``muni_seq`` and ``settlement_seq`` ``n`` (see :data:`_PART_CONT_RE`). Before
    this, the continuation stayed inside the first part's text and every
    institution after it was filed under part 1. ``index`` still runs in printed
    order, so :func:`join_symbols`, which orders a municipality's markers by
    ``(entry_index, position)``, sees exactly the sequence it saw before.

    **Both printed forms of that marker** (0.7.0). A part that opens a new line is
    printed as a bare ``n)`` with no dash; :func:`_open_line_part` restores the
    dash while the line is folded into its municipality, so it splits here too.
    """
    entries: list[Entry] = []
    for chunk in _entry_chunks(section):
        marks = list(_ENTRY_KEY_RE.finditer(chunk))
        for i, mark in enumerate(marks):
            end = marks[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(marks) else len(chunk)
            printed = mark.group(1)
            value = int(printed)
            # Non-monotonic is a misread digit; a *gap* is not. Flagged, never
            # overwritten — see the note above on why the old repair was pure loss.
            # Judged once per printed municipality number, before its parts are
            # appended: a continuation repeats the number by construction.
            suspect = bool(entries) and value <= entries[-1].muni_seq
            parts = _split_parts(chunk[mark.end():end],
                                 _settlement_seq(mark.group(2)))
            previous = int(parts[0][0]) if parts[0][0].isdigit() else None
            for k, (settlement, text) in enumerate(parts):
                # A part number that does not rise is the same kind of evidence as a
                # municipality number that goes backwards: usually a later key the
                # OCR destroyed, so its parts were folded in here. Over the text
                # layer of the whole volume 28 of 527 multi-part municipalities do
                # this. Flagged, never renumbered.
                backwards = (k > 0 and previous is not None
                             and int(settlement) <= previous)
                if k > 0:
                    previous = int(settlement)
                entries.append(Entry(
                    district=section.key, page=section.page,
                    muni_seq=value, settlement_seq=settlement,
                    text=text.strip(" .,;"),
                    index=len(entries), seq_printed=printed,
                    seq_repaired=(suspect and k == 0) or backwards))
    return entries


def _spells_coop_letter(match: re.Match, text: str, coop_letter: re.Pattern) -> bool:
    """Whether a word code's match is, as printed, a whole-word cooperative letter and no
    more: ``Sch,`` and ``Gb`` are, ``S. D.`` (which begins with one) is not."""
    word = re.match(r"[^\W\d_]+", text[match.start():])
    return (bool(word) and coop_letter.fullmatch(word.group(0)) is not None
            and len(match.group(0).rstrip(". ")) <= len(word.group(0)))


def decode_entry(entry: Entry, abbreviations: list[Abbreviation]) -> list[dict]:
    """Everything one entry records: decoded abbreviations plus unresolved glyphs.

    Matches are consumed as they are found so a long code is not re-reported by a
    shorter one nested inside it, and the remaining glyph runs are emitted as
    ``icon`` rows with an empty ``code`` for the vision pass to fill.

    **Consumed by blanking, not by deleting, and the difference is the join.** A
    match used to be replaced by a single space, which shortened the string, so
    every offset after it moved and the glyph runs found later carried positions
    into a string that no longer existed. Blanking the span keeps every position
    true to ``entry.text``, which is what lets the k-th unresolved marker here be
    identified with the k-th named symbol a vision pass returns for the same
    entry — see :func:`join_symbols`. The records are returned in **printed
    order** for the same reason; they used to come back in abbreviation-table
    order, which is an artefact of the loop rather than a fact about the page.
    """
    remaining = entry.text
    found: list[dict] = []
    coop_letter = _coop_letter_re(abbreviations)

    for abbrev in abbreviations:
        if abbrev.kind in ("qualifier", "unit"):
            continue
        pattern = _pattern_for(abbrev)
        matches = [m for m in pattern.finditer(remaining)
                   if _is_coop_letter(abbrev) or coop_letter is None
                   or not _spells_coop_letter(m, remaining, coop_letter)]
        for match in matches:
            before = remaining[max(0, match.start() - 4):match.start()]
            count = _COUNT_RE.search(before)
            suffix = _COOP_SUFFIX_RE.match(remaining[match.start():])
            # A single letter is a cooperative only where the source puts one: in
            # the list that follows the družstvo pictogram and its colon
            # (``&■=: R; K``). Elsewhere a lone capital is glyph noise, and
            # accepting it invents institutions. Kept as low confidence rather
            # than dropped, so the judgement stays visible in the output.
            confidence = "high"
            if abbrev.kind == "cooperative" and len(abbrev.key) <= 3:
                confidence = ("high" if ":" in remaining[:match.start()]
                              else "low")
            found.append({
                "confidence": confidence,
                "check": "I10_institution", "district": entry.district,
                "page": entry.page, "muni_seq": entry.muni_seq,
                "entry_index": entry.index,
                "settlement_seq": entry.settlement_seq,
                "source": "abbrev", "code": abbrev.code,
                "expansion": abbrev.expansion, "english": abbrev.english,
                "category": abbrev.category,
                "count": int(count.group(1)) if count else 1,
                "language_suffix": (suffix.group(2) if suffix else ""),
                "position": match.start(),
                "glyph": "", "context": remaining[max(0, match.start() - 12):
                                                  match.end() + 12].strip(),
            })
        for match in matches:
            remaining = (remaining[:match.start()] + " " * (match.end() - match.start())
                         + remaining[match.end():])

    for match in _GLYPH_RE.finditer(remaining):
        found.append({
            "check": "I10_institution", "district": entry.district,
            "page": entry.page, "muni_seq": entry.muni_seq,
            "settlement_seq": entry.settlement_seq,
            "entry_index": entry.index,
            "source": "icon", "code": "", "expansion": "", "english": "",
            "category": "", "count": 1, "language_suffix": "",
            "position": match.start(),
            "confidence": "unresolved", "glyph": match.group(0),
            "context": entry.text[max(0, match.start() - 12):
                                  match.end() + 12].strip(),
        })
    return sorted(found, key=lambda r: r["position"])


def decode_sections(sections, abbreviations) -> tuple[list[dict], list[Entry]]:
    """Decode every offices section. Returns ``(records, entries)``."""
    records: list[dict] = []
    entries: list[Entry] = []
    for section in sections:
        if section.kind != "offices":
            continue
        for entry in parse_entries(section):
            entries.append(entry)
            records += decode_entry(entry, abbreviations)
    return records, entries


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# I11 — filling the text layer's slots from a named-symbol pass
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#
# The text layer knows a marker was printed and where; it cannot know which one.
# A vision pass over the same section knows which one but is a worse reader of the
# words around it. The join is therefore positional and per entry: the k-th
# unresolved marker in a municipality's entry is the k-th named symbol the model
# returned for that municipality's entry.
#
# **The count is the whole guard.** Nothing here can tell whether [school] is the
# right name for the third glyph in Brzice's line — there is no arithmetic down
# here and no gold standard. What it *can* tell is whether the two channels agree
# that Brzice's line has four markers in it. If they do not, the k-th of one is
# not the k-th of the other and every name after the discrepancy would be attached
# to the wrong institution, so the entry is refused whole rather than joined up to
# the point where they diverge. A refusal leaves an unresolved slot, which is what
# was there before; a silent misalignment invents an inventory.

#: A named symbol from the vision pass: the bracketed tokens of the closed list.
#: Ordinary abbreviations are excluded — both channels read those from the text
#: and the text layer's reading is the better one.
_SYMBOL_CODE_RE = re.compile(r"^\[[^\]]+\]$")


def _entry_key(record: dict) -> tuple:
    """Which entry a decoded marker belongs to: **its printed municipality number**.

    Two wrong answers preceded this one, and both are worth keeping in view.

    Keying on ``(muni_seq, settlement_seq)`` matched 20 of qwen3.5's 545 named
    symbols. The cause turned out not to be the key but the number: ``parse_entries``
    was rewriting legible printed figures onto a consecutive run, so the text layer
    reported 1..12 where the page prints 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15.
    The two channels were reading the same digits and being given different ones.

    Aligning by *position in the section* instead made it worse — 4 markers — because
    position is only stable while both channels cut the section into the same number
    of entries, and they do not: the cut runs off the model's own line breaks, so an
    entry it wraps differently shifts every entry after it. Sixteen of thirty-one
    sections were refused outright.

    With the fabricated numbers gone, the printed figure is the right key after all.
    It is what both channels actually read, it survives one channel dropping or
    inserting an entry — that entry simply goes unjoined instead of offsetting its
    neighbours — and where a digit really is misread the entry drops out rather than
    attaching to someone else.

    ``settlement_seq`` is deliberately **not** in the key. It is a single character
    in the most damaged column on the page, and the channels disagree on it
    constantly (the ALTO's ``i`` against the model's ``1``). A municipality's
    sub-entries are therefore pooled and their markers ordered by
    ``(entry_index, position)``, which is the printed order within the municipality.
    """
    return (record.get("page", ""), record.get("district", ""),
            record.get("muni_seq"))


def join_symbols(alto_records: list[dict], vision_records: list[dict],
                 unknown: str = "[?]",
                 count_unnamed: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """Name the text layer's unresolved markers from a vision pass over the same
    sections. Returns one record per marker, joined or refused.

    Both sides are taken in printed order within an entry, which
    :func:`decode_entry` now guarantees. An entry the vision pass never reached is
    reported as ``only_text`` rather than dropped: an institution inventory that
    quietly omits the municipalities nobody read is the same lie as one that omits
    the municipalities with no post office.

    ``count_unnamed`` includes the image read's *own* unresolved marks on the
    right-hand side, as markers seen but not named. Off by default and on for a
    **transcription** pass, and the distinction is not cosmetic. A dedicated OCR
    model asked only to transcribe renders every pictogram as one placeholder, so
    it names nothing and its side of the join is empty — which reported all 98
    entries of the glm-ocr control as "no image read reached the entry" when it
    had read every one of them. That wasted the control: its whole purpose is to
    test whether an independent reader *counts* the markers in an entry the way
    the text layer does, which is the precondition for any naming pass, and it can
    answer that without naming anything.

    It stays off for an annotating pass, where a leftover glyph is stray
    punctuation the reader emitted rather than a mark it saw, and counting those
    would invent disagreements.

    """
    slots: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    for record in alto_records:
        if record.get("source") == "icon":
            slots.setdefault(_entry_key(record), []).append(record)

    named: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    for record in vision_records:
        if (record.get("source") == "abbrev"
                and _SYMBOL_CODE_RE.match(str(record.get("code", "")))):
            named.setdefault(_entry_key(record), []).append(record)
        elif count_unnamed and record.get("source") == "icon":
            named.setdefault(_entry_key(record), []).append(
                {**record, "code": unknown})

    # No section-level guard here. It was needed while entries aligned by
    # position, where one extra entry offset every entry after it; a printed
    # number cannot be offset by its neighbours, so a section the two channels cut
    # differently now costs the entries that differ and nothing else.
    joined: list[dict] = []

    for key in sorted(set(slots) | set(named), key=lambda k: tuple(map(str, k))):
        page, district, muni_seq = key
        order = lambda r: (r.get("entry_index", 0), r["position"])
        left = sorted(slots.get(key, []), key=order)
        right = sorted(named.get(key, []), key=order)
        # The municipality number comes from the text layer, which is the
        # numbering the rest of the pipeline joins on. The image read's own
        # reading of it is carried beside it as evidence, never as the key.
        settlement_seq = (left or right)[0].get("settlement_seq", "")
        base = {"check": "I11_symbol_join", "page": page, "district": district,
                "muni_seq": muni_seq,
                "entry_index": (left or right)[0].get("entry_index", ""),
                "settlement_seq": settlement_seq,
                "muni_seq_image": (right[0].get("muni_seq", "") if right else ""),
                "n_text_slots": len(left), "n_named": len(right)}
        if not right:
            joined.append({**base, "verdict": "only_text", "position": "",
                           "glyph": "", "code": "", "english": "", "category": "",
                           "detail": "no vision read reached this entry"})
            continue
        if not left:
            joined.append({**base, "verdict": "only_image", "position": "",
                           "glyph": "", "code": "", "english": "", "category": "",
                           "detail": "the text layer found no marker here — the "
                                     "image read may have named something the "
                                     "engine rendered as an ordinary character"})
            continue
        if len(left) != len(right):
            joined.append({
                **base, "verdict": "count_mismatch", "position": "", "glyph": "",
                "code": "", "english": "", "category": "",
                "detail": f"{len(left)} markers in the text layer against "
                          f"{len(right)} named in the image — the k-th of one is "
                          f"not the k-th of the other, so none are joined"})
            continue
        for slot, name in zip(left, right):
            unplaced = name["code"] == unknown
            joined.append({
                **base,
                # Each marker keeps the part it was printed under (0.5.0); `base`
                # carries the municipality's first part, which is right only for
                # the rows that are about the whole municipality. The image read's
                # part is preferred: it is the channel that reads the digit cleanly.
                "settlement_seq": (name.get("settlement_seq")
                                   or slot.get("settlement_seq", "")
                                   or base["settlement_seq"]),
                "verdict": "unplaced" if unplaced else "joined",
                "position": slot["position"], "glyph": slot["glyph"],
                "code": name["code"], "english": name.get("english", ""),
                "category": name.get("category", ""),
                "count": name.get("count", 1),
                "context": slot.get("context", ""),
                "detail": "" if not unplaced else
                          "the reader saw a symbol it could not place on the list",
            })
    return joined


def lexikon_1910_join_report(joined: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for I11."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_institutions v{__version__} — I11, naming the text "
             f"layer's markers from the image", ""]
    if not joined:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  nothing to join — no vision pass over these "
                                  "sections"])
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for record in joined:
        counts[record["verdict"]] = counts.get(record["verdict"], 0) + 1
    entries = len({(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"],
                    r["settlement_seq"]) for r in joined})
    lines.append(f"  {entries} municipality entries considered")
    for verdict, label in (("joined", "marker named"),
                           ("unplaced", "symbol seen, not on the list"),
                           ("count_mismatch", "counts differ — entry refused"),

                           ("only_text", "no image read reached the entry"),
                           ("only_image", "named where the text layer saw no mark")):
        if counts.get(verdict):
            lines.append(f"    {label:38s} {counts[verdict]:5d}")

    placed = [r for r in joined if r["verdict"] == "joined"]
    if placed:
        by_cat: dict[str, int] = {}
        for record in placed:
            by_cat[record["category"]] = by_cat.get(record["category"], 0) + 1
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  named markers by category:")
        for cat, n in sorted(by_cat.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
            lines.append(f"    {cat or '(uncategorised)':16s} {n:5d}")
    slots = sum(int(r["n_text_slots"]) for r in joined
                if str(r.get("n_text_slots", "")).isdigit())
    seen = sum(int(r["n_named"]) for r in joined
               if str(r.get("n_named", "")).isdigit())
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"  markers: text layer {slots}, image read {seen}"
                 + (f"  ({seen / slots:.1f}x)" if slots else ""))
    lines.append("  A large excess on the image side is expected and is NOT a "
                 "reader error. The text")
    lines.append("  layer can only see a pictogram the OCR turned into a "
                 "non-letter; one rendered as")
    lines.append("  'g' or 'f' is invisible to it. Over the pilot it saw about a "
                 "third of what was")
    lines.append("  printed, so 'counts differ' is the normal case here and the "
                 "count cannot gate the")
    lines.append("  inventory — only two independent readers agreeing can (I12).")
    return "\n".join(lines)



# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# I14 — which place each entry is about
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#
# The entry key is two numbers and the register prints them in two weights. The
# **bold** figure is the municipality's running number in the soudní okres and
# matches the bold number in column 1 of the table above; the **light** figure is
# the settlement's number within that municipality and matches the light numbers
# beneath it. So ``1, 1)`` in okres Česká Skalice is municipality 1, settlement 1
# — Brzice, Brzice — and ``2, —)`` is municipality 2 taken whole, Červená Hora.
#
# Nothing in this module could say that from the footnote alone, and without it the
# inventory is a list of institutions attached to numbers. This is the join that
# makes it a **place-level covariate**: every institution acquires the name of the
# obec or osada it belonged to, and through that everything the rest of the
# pipeline knows about that place.
#
# Weight is not detectable in the ALTO and is not needed: position in the key
# already says which number is which.


def place_index(blocks_by_court) -> dict:
    """``(court, muni_seq, settlement_seq) -> the printed table row``.

    ``settlement_seq`` ``"0"`` is the municipality's own line, which is what the
    printed dash means — see :func:`_settlement_seq`. A settlement carries its own
    number, restarting at 1 inside every municipality.
    """
    from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910 as lx

    index: dict = {}
    for court, blocks in (blocks_by_court or {}).items():
        for block in blocks:
            muni, status = lx.parse_int_cell(block.municipality.get("seq"))
            if status != "ok" or muni is None:
                # Column 1 is the most damaged text on the page. An unreadable
                # municipality number means this block cannot be addressed, which
                # is reported by absence rather than by a guessed number.
                continue
            index[(court, muni, "0")] = block.municipality
            for position, row in enumerate(block.settlements, start=1):
                seq, seq_status = lx.parse_int_cell(row.get("seq"))
                # Read where legible, else fall back to the printed order, which
                # for settlements *is* the numbering — they run 1..n with no gaps
                # inside a municipality, unlike the municipalities themselves.
                index[(court, muni, str(seq if seq_status == "ok" else position))] = row
    return index


def _place_name(row) -> str:
    """The Czech name of a printed row, without the German twin or the symbols."""
    name = (row.get("name") or "").split(",")[0]
    return re.sub(r"[^\w\s.\-]", " ", name, flags=re.UNICODE).strip()


def attach_places(rows: list[dict], index: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Give every inventory row the place its entry is about.

    Adds ``place_name`` and ``place_level`` (``municipality`` / ``settlement``),
    and leaves them empty where the join fails rather than falling back to the
    municipality — an institution recorded against a settlement is a fact about
    that settlement, and quietly promoting it to the obec would move it.
    """
    for row in rows:
        key = (row.get("district", ""), row.get("muni_seq"),
               str(row.get("settlement_seq", "") or "0"))
        try:
            key = (key[0], int(key[1]), key[2])
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            row["place_name"] = ""
            row["place_level"] = ""
            continue
        found = index.get(key)
        row["place_name"] = _place_name(found) if found is not None else ""
        row["place_level"] = ("" if found is None else
                              "municipality" if key[2] == "0" else "settlement")
    return rows


def lexikon_1910_places_joined_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for I14."""
    lines = ["lexikon_1910_institutions v" + __version__
             + " — I14, the place each entry is about", ""]
    if not rows:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  nothing to join"])
    named = [r for r in rows if r.get("place_name")]
    entries = {(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"]) for r in rows}
    placed = {(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"]) for r in named}
    lines.append(f"  {len(rows)} inventory rows over {len(entries)} entries")
    lines.append(f"  rows given a place name: {len(named)} "
                 f"({len(named) / len(rows):.1%})")
    lines.append(f"  entries resolved to a place: {len(placed)}/{len(entries)} "
                 f"({len(placed) / max(len(entries), 1):.1%})")
    levels: dict = {}
    for row in named:
        levels[row["place_level"]] = levels.get(row["place_level"], 0) + 1
    for level, n in sorted(levels.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
        lines.append(f"    {level:14s} {n:5d}")
    sample = [r for r in named][:6]
    if sample:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  sample:")
        for row in sample:
            lines.append(f"    {row['district'][:16]:16s} "
                         f"{row['muni_seq']}, {row.get('settlement_seq') or '0'}) "
                         f"{row['place_name'][:26]:26s} {row['code']}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("  An entry that resolves to nothing is one whose municipality "
                 "number the table")
    lines.append("  could not be read at, not one whose institutions are in doubt. "
                 "It is left empty")
    lines.append("  rather than promoted to the obec, which would move a "
                 "settlement's institution.")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# I13 — the inventory itself, read from the image
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#
# This is the offices inventory the pipeline should use, and the channel it comes
# from is the *image*, not the text layer. That inverts what this module was built
# to do, and the measurement in the module docstring is why: the ALTO emits 291
# markers where the readers find 545 and 893, because it can only recognise a
# pictogram that OCR'd into a non-letter. It is not a complete locator, so it
# cannot be the record.
#
# What it remains excellent at is everything set in ordinary type — ``o. s.``,
# ``notář``, ``b. úř.``, ``2 měšť. šk.`` — and the municipality numbers, which are
# baseline digits. So the two channels swap roles rather than one replacing the
# other: the image read supplies the inventory, the text layer supplies the
# scaffold it hangs on and corroborates every code it can also see.
#
# **The corroboration rate on text-readable codes is the quality signal**, and it
# is worth more than it looks. Both channels can read ``notář`` off the same ink by
# completely different machinery, so the share of the text layer's abbreviations
# that the image read also found measures the reader's transcription accuracy
# *without needing a legend* — and a reader that transcribes the words well is the
# one whose symbol names are worth having. It is the only accuracy number available
# here until the Výklad značek plate is transcribed.


def build_inventory(vision_records: list[dict],
                    alto_records: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """The offices inventory, image read primary, text layer corroborating.

    One row per (entry, code). ``source`` says which channels found it:

    ``both``   the image read it and the text layer decoded it too. For an
               ordinary abbreviation this is the corroborated case.
    ``image``  only the image read has it. Every pictogram is here by definition —
               the text layer cannot name one — and so is anything the OCR mangled
               past recognition.
    ``text``   only the text layer has it: the image read missed a code the OCR
               got. Kept, because dropping it would make the inventory worse than
               either channel alone, and flagged, because it is also where the
               image reader is weakest.

    Counts are taken from the channel that owns the row, and disagreement between
    the two on a shared code is recorded in ``count_text`` rather than resolved.
    """
    def index(records):
        out: dict[tuple, dict[str, list[dict]]] = {}
        for record in records:
            if record.get("source") not in ("abbrev", "icon"):
                continue
            entry = out.setdefault(_entry_key(record), {})
            entry.setdefault(str(record.get("code", "")), []).append(record)
        return out

    right, left = index(vision_records), index(alto_records)
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for key in sorted(set(right) | set(left), key=lambda k: tuple(map(str, k))):
        page, district, muni_seq = key
        g_codes, b_codes = right.get(key, {}), left.get(key, {})
        for code in sorted(set(g_codes) | set(b_codes)):
            in_g, in_b = code in g_codes, code in b_codes
