            # An unresolved mark is not a code and cannot be corroborated by one.
            if not code:
                for record in g_codes.get(code, []):
                    rows.append(_inventory_row(record, page, district, muni_seq,
                                               "image", corroborated=False))
                continue
            source = "both" if in_g and in_b else ("image" if in_g else "text")
            owned = (g_codes if in_g else b_codes)[code]
            # ONE ROW PER PART, not per municipality (0.5.0). Grouping on the
            # municipality alone took the first record's `settlement_seq` for all
            # of them, so a fire brigade printed under parts 1 and 2 became one row
            # on part 1 — the settlement-level half of D-56. The part is the owning
            # channel's reading; corroboration stays municipality-level, because
            # the two channels disagree on the part character itself (`i` / `1`).
            by_part: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
            for record in owned:
                by_part.setdefault(str(record.get("settlement_seq", "")),
                                   []).append(record)
            for part, records in by_part.items():
                row = _inventory_row(records[0], page, district, muni_seq, source,
                                     corroborated=in_g and in_b)
                row["count"] = sum(r.get("count", 1) for r in records)
                if not in_b:
                    row["count_text"] = ""
                elif len(by_part) == 1:
                    # The common case, and exactly what 0.4.0 recorded.
                    row["count_text"] = sum(r.get("count", 1) for r in b_codes[code])
                else:
                    # Several parts: the text layer's count for *this* part where its
                    # part reading agrees, blank where it does not — never the
                    # municipality total repeated on every row.
                    same = [r for r in b_codes[code]
                            if str(r.get("settlement_seq", "")) == part]
                    row["count_text"] = (sum(r.get("count", 1) for r in same)
                                         if same else "")
                rows.append(row)
    return rows


def _inventory_row(record: dict, page, district, muni_seq, source: str,
                   corroborated: bool) -> dict:
    return {"check": "I13_inventory", "page": page, "district": district,
            "muni_seq": muni_seq, "entry_index": record.get("entry_index", ""),
            "settlement_seq": record.get("settlement_seq", ""),
            "code": record.get("code", ""),
            "expansion": record.get("expansion", ""),
            "english": record.get("english", ""),
            "category": record.get("category", ""),
            "count": record.get("count", 1), "count_text": "",
            "source": source, "corroborated": corroborated,
            "confidence": record.get("confidence", ""),
            "glyph": record.get("glyph", ""),
            "context": record.get("context", "")}


def lexikon_1910_inventory_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for I13."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_institutions v{__version__} — I13, the offices "
             f"inventory (image read primary)", ""]
    if not rows:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  nothing read"])
    by_source: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in rows:
        by_source[row["source"]] = by_source.get(row["source"], 0) + 1
    entries = len({(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"]) for r in rows})
    lines.append(f"  {len(rows)} inventory rows over {entries} municipality "
                 f"entries")
    for source, label in (("both", "image + text layer agree"),
                          ("image", "image read only"),
                          ("text", "text layer only — the image read missed it")):
        if by_source.get(source):
            lines.append(f"    {label:44s} {by_source[source]:5d}")

    symbols = [r for r in rows if str(r["code"]).startswith("[")]
    unresolved = [r for r in rows if not r["code"]]
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"  named pictograms: {len(symbols)}   "
                 f"unresolved marks still carried: {len(unresolved)}")

    # The one accuracy figure available without a transcribed legend.
    words = [r for r in rows
             if r["code"] and not str(r["code"]).startswith("[")]
    shared = [r for r in words if r["source"] in ("both", "text")]
    agreed = [r for r in shared if r["source"] == "both"]
    if shared:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"  corroboration on codes BOTH channels can read: "
                     f"{len(agreed)}/{len(shared)} = "
                     f"{len(agreed) / len(shared):.1%}")
        lines.append("    These are the ordinary abbreviations — o. s., notář, "
                     "b. úř. — which the text")
        lines.append("    layer reads well. Two different machineries on the same "
                     "ink, so this measures")
        lines.append("    the image reader's transcription without needing a "
                     "legend, and a reader that")
        lines.append("    transcribes well is the one whose symbol names are worth "
                     "having.")

    by_cat: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in rows:
        if row["code"]:
            by_cat[row["category"]] = by_cat.get(row["category"], 0) + row["count"]
    if by_cat:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  inventory by category:")
        for cat, n in sorted(by_cat.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
            lines.append(f"    {cat or '(uncategorised)':16s} {n:5d}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# I12 — one marker, several readers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#
# I11 asks whether a reader's names can be attached to the text layer's markers.
# I12 asks whether two readers, given the same marker, say the same thing.
#
# **The marker key is what makes this work, and it comes from neither reader.** A
# joined record is addressed by (page, district, municipality, settlement,
# position), and every one of those is the *text layer's*: the same deterministic
# parse runs in both passes, so both are pointing at the same ink. Two readers can
# therefore be compared glyph by glyph rather than line by line, which is the only
# comparison worth making — the words around a symbol are where they legitimately
# differ, and the symbol is where one of them is wrong.
#
# Agreement is evidence and not proof, and weaker evidence here than elsewhere in
# this pipeline. Two vision models trained on overlapping corpora can share a
# misreading, and the closed list makes that likelier rather than less: both are
# choosing from the same 56 tokens, so a glyph that resembles the wrong one
# resembles it for both. What this *does* establish is a worklist. A marker two
# readers disagree about is a marker worth a human's time, and there are far fewer
# of those than there are markers.

#: What a reader emits for a symbol it could not place. Not a disagreement.
UNPLACED = "[?]"


def compare_inventories(passes: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
    """Agreement between passes on **what each entry contains**, not on markers.

    This is the comparison that works, and the marker-level one below is kept only
    for the case where positions exist. :func:`join_symbols` can only surface a
    marker where the text layer also has a slot *and* the two counts match, and
    since the text layer holds about a third of the markers, each pass surfaces a
    different small subset. Over the 20-page pilot that left 57 markers and made
    qwen's and gemma's contributions almost disjoint — so the comparison reported
    **no disagreements at all** while the true rate was around 86%. A check that
    can only see where two readers overlap by construction will always report
    agreement, which is the worst failure available to a check whose job is to
    find conflict.

    So this runs on the I13 inventories, which hold everything each pass read. The
    unit is ``(entry, code)``: did this pass claim this institution for this
    municipality? Positions are neither needed nor available there, which is the
    price — two readers that both say ``[school]`` for an entry agree here even if
    they attached it to different marks. That is the right trade while the naming
    is this unreliable: which institutions a place had is the covariate, and which
    glyph carried it is not.

    Only entries **every** pass read are compared. Elsewhere a missing claim means
    "not read", not "disagreed", and pooling the two would score coverage as
    conflict.
    """
    # A pass that names nothing cannot agree or disagree about a name. Counting
    # a transcription pass among the voters makes unanimity arithmetically
    # impossible and reports 0.0% as though it were a measurement — the same shape
    # of error as a check whose denominator decides its own answer. Such a pass is
    # still read for *coverage*, so it still constrains which entries count.
    labels = sorted(lab for lab, rows in passes.items()
                    if any(str(r.get("code", "")).startswith("[") for r in rows))
    claims: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
    seen: dict[str, set] = {lab: set() for lab in passes}
    for label, rows in passes.items():
        for row in rows:
            entry = (row.get("page", ""), row.get("district", ""),
                     row.get("muni_seq"))
            seen[label].add(entry)
            code = str(row.get("code", ""))
            if not code.startswith("["):        # symbols only
                continue
            slot = claims.setdefault(entry + (code,),
                                     {"by": {}, "category": "", "english": ""})
            if label in labels:
                slot["by"][label] = int(row.get("count", 1) or 1)
            slot["category"] = row.get("category", "")
            slot["english"] = row.get("english", "")
    shared = set.intersection(*seen.values()) if seen else set()

    out: list[dict] = []
    for key in sorted(claims, key=lambda k: tuple(map(str, k))):
        page, district, muni_seq, code = key
        if (page, district, muni_seq) not in shared:
            continue
        slot = claims[key]
        record = {"check": "I12_inventory_agreement", "page": page,
                  "district": district, "muni_seq": muni_seq, "code": code,
                  "english": slot["english"], "category": slot["category"],
                  "n_claiming": len(slot["by"]), "n_passes": len(labels),
                  "verdict": ("unanimous" if len(slot["by"]) == len(labels)
                              else "contested")}
        for label in labels:
            record["count_" + label] = slot["by"].get(label, "")
        out.append(record)
    return out


def lexikon_1910_inventory_agreement_report(records, labels) -> str:
    """Ledger for the inventory-level comparison."""
    lines = ["lexikon_1910_institutions v" + __version__ + " — I12, what "
             + str(len(labels)) + " passes say each entry contains", ""]
    if not records:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  no entry was read by every pass"])
    lines.append("  naming passes: " + ", ".join(labels))
    unan = [r for r in records if r["verdict"] == "unanimous"]
    entries = len({(r["page"], r["district"], r["muni_seq"]) for r in records})
    lines.append(f"  {len(records)} (entry, symbol) claims over {entries} "
                 f"municipality entries that every pass read")
    lines.append(f"    every pass claims it   {len(unan):5d}  "
                 f"{len(unan) / len(records):5.1%}")
    lines.append(f"    only some do           {len(records) - len(unan):5d}  "
                 f"{1 - len(unan) / len(records):5.1%}")
    for label in labels:
        mine = sum(1 for r in records if r.get("count_" + label) != "")
        lines.append(f"    {label:12s} claims {mine:5d} of them")
    contested: dict[str, int] = {}
    for record in records:
        if record["verdict"] != "unanimous":
            contested[record["code"]] = contested.get(record["code"], 0) + 1
    if contested:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("  most contested symbols (claimed by some passes, not all):")
        for code, n in sorted(contested.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:12]:
            lines.append(f"    {n:4d}x  {code}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("  Low unanimity here is a statement about the *naming*, not "
                 "about the readers'")
    lines.append("  eyesight: all of them transcribe the words of these entries "
                 "well. They are being")
    lines.append("  asked to map a printed 1916 glyph onto an English description "
                 "they have never")
    lines.append("  seen drawn. That is what the symbol atlas is for.")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Accuracy against a transcriber, as opposed to agreement between readers.
#
# :func:`compare_inventories` answers "do the readers say the same thing", and it
# has to score only the entries *every* pass read — which collapses toward zero
# as passes are added. That is right for unanimity and wrong for accuracy: when
# one of the passes is a person, the question is not what the field agrees on but
# how close each reader is to the person, and that comparison is **pairwise**. A
# pass is scored on the entries it and the transcriber both read, so adding a
# tenth model does not shrink the ninth model's denominator.
#
# Coverage is reported beside accuracy rather than folded into it. An entry the
# transcriber read and the reader never reached is a miss of a different kind
# from an entry it read and named wrongly, and averaging the two hides which
# lever — crop geometry or symbol naming — a pass actually needs.


def _entry_of(row: dict) -> tuple:
    """The unit :func:`compare_inventories` uses: one municipality entry."""
    return (row.get("page", ""), row.get("district", ""), row.get("muni_seq"))


def _claims(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[set, set]:
    """``(entries read, (entry, code) claims)`` for one pass."""
    entries, claims = set(), set()
    for row in rows:
        entry = _entry_of(row)
        entries.add(entry)
        code = str(row.get("code", "") or "")
        if code.startswith("[") and code != UNPLACED:
            claims.add(entry + (code,))
    return entries, claims


#: The two units a claim can be keyed on. ``settlement`` is the analysis unit —
#: the covariate is what one part of a municipality had — and since 0.6.0 it is
#: the headline (D-56). ``municipality`` is the unit every figure before
#: 2026-09-22 was reported on, kept beside it so the old numbers stay comparable.
LEVELS = ("municipality", "settlement")

#: Coverage of the page-clustered interval, and the tail it leaves on each side.
INTERVAL = 0.95
_TAIL = (1 - INTERVAL) / 2

#: Seed for the page bootstrap: the same one ``run_e1_gemini_version.py`` draws
#: its entry bootstrap with, so the two reports are reproducible together.
BOOTSTRAP_SEED = 1910

#: The part a municipality-wide claim is filed under (a printed dash, see
#: :func:`_settlement_seq`).
WHOLE = "0"


def _count_of(row: dict) -> int:
    """The printed count on a claim; a blank or unreadable one counts once."""
    try:
        return max(int(str(row.get("count", "") or 1)), 1)
    except ValueError:
        return 1


def _part_of(row: dict) -> str:
    """The part a claim is filed under.

    A blank is read as :data:`WHOLE`. That pools "no separate settlement" with
    "the part figure was lost", which :func:`_settlement_seq` keeps apart — but
    it is the key the 2026-09-23 settlement figure (0.915) was measured with,
    and a scorer that keyed differently would not reproduce it.
    """
    return str(row.get("settlement_seq") or WHOLE)


def _claim_counts(rows: list[dict],
                  level: str = "settlement") -> tuple[set, set, dict]:
    """``(entries read, units seen, {claim: printed count})`` for one pass.

    A claim is ``unit + (code,)``, where the unit is the entry at
    ``municipality`` level and ``entry + (part,)`` at ``settlement`` level. So
    ``claim[:3]`` is always the entry, ``claim[:-1]`` the unit and ``claim[-1]``
    the code. ``units`` holds every unit the pass has a row for, claimed symbol
    or not — the denominator a specificity needs.
    """
    if level not in LEVELS:
        raise ValueError(f"level must be one of {LEVELS}, not {level!r}")
    entries, units, claims = set(), set(), {}
    for row in rows:
        entry = _entry_of(row)
        entries.add(entry)
        unit = entry + (_part_of(row),) if level == "settlement" else entry
        units.add(unit)
        code = str(row.get("code", "") or "")
        if code.startswith("[") and code != UNPLACED:
            claims[unit + (code,)] = claims.get(unit + (code,), 0) + _count_of(row)
    return entries, units, claims


def describe_reference(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """What a reference pass covers, counted from its rows rather than typed.

    Every report that names the gold prints this, so the line cannot go on saying
    "4 pages, 280 claims" after the gold has changed underneath it.
    """
    entries, _units, claims = _claim_counts(rows, "settlement")
    _entries, _units, at_muni = _claim_counts(rows, "municipality")
    pages = sorted({str(entry[0]) for entry in entries})
    return (f"{len(pages)} pages ({', '.join(pages)}), {len(entries)} entries, "
            f"{len(claims)} claims at settlement level, {len(at_muni)} at "
            f"municipality level")


def _prf(hit: int, false: int, missed: int) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Precision, recall and F1 from the three counts."""
    precision = hit / (hit + false) if hit + false else 0.0
    recall = hit / (hit + missed) if hit + missed else 0.0
    f1 = (2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
          if precision + recall else 0.0)
    return precision, recall, f1


def _shared_claims(reference_rows: list[dict], rows: list[dict],
                   level: str) -> tuple[set, set, dict, dict]:
    """Both sides' claims restricted to the entries both read.

    Returns ``(shared entries, units either side saw, reference claims, pass
    claims)``, the last two as ``{claim: count}``.
    """
    ref_entries, ref_units, ref = _claim_counts(reference_rows, level)
    entries, my_units, mine = _claim_counts(rows, level)
    shared = ref_entries & entries
    units = {u for u in ref_units | my_units if u[:3] in shared}
    return (shared, units,
            {c: n for c, n in ref.items() if c[:3] in shared},
            {c: n for c, n in mine.items() if c[:3] in shared})


def _settlement_scores(reference_rows: list[dict], rows: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """The settlement-level block of one pass's row in the accuracy table.

    ``false_misfiled`` and ``missed_misfiled`` are the claims that are wrong
    *only* in the part: the reader named an institution the municipality does
    have and filed it under a part the reference does not, or the reverse. They
    are what separates the settlement figure from the municipality one, and
    :func:`part_attribution` lists them.

    Counts are scored twice, and neither replaces presence. ``count_exact`` is
    the share of hits whose printed count also matches. ``f1_count`` weights
    each claim by its count — a hit is ``min`` of the two counts — so two
    schools read as one costs half a claim instead of nothing.
    """
    _shared, _units, theirs, mine = _shared_claims(reference_rows, rows,
                                                   "settlement")
    hit = mine.keys() & theirs.keys()
    false, missed = mine.keys() - theirs.keys(), theirs.keys() - mine.keys()
    at_muni = lambda claims: {c[:3] + (c[-1],) for c in claims}
    ref_muni, my_muni = at_muni(theirs), at_muni(mine)
    precision, recall, f1 = _prf(len(hit), len(false), len(missed))
    hit_n = sum(min(mine[c], theirs[c]) for c in hit)
    _pc, _rc, f1_count = _prf(hit_n, sum(mine.values()) - hit_n,
                              sum(theirs.values()) - hit_n)
    count_agree = sum(1 for c in hit if mine[c] == theirs[c])
    return {
        "reference_claims_settlement": len(theirs),
        "claims_settlement": len(mine),
        "hit_settlement": len(hit), "false_settlement": len(false),
        "missed_settlement": len(missed),
        "false_misfiled": sum(1 for c in false
                              if c[:3] + (c[-1],) in ref_muni),
        "missed_misfiled": sum(1 for c in missed
                               if c[:3] + (c[-1],) in my_muni),
        "precision_settlement": round(precision, 3),
        "recall_settlement": round(recall, 3),
        "f1_settlement": round(f1, 3),
        "count_agree": count_agree,
        "count_exact": round(count_agree / len(hit), 3) if hit else 0.0,
        "f1_count": round(f1_count, 3),
    }


def score_against_reference(passes: dict[str, list[dict]],
                            reference: str = "human") -> list[dict]:
    """Precision and recall of each pass against one pass taken as truth.

    **Two units, side by side (0.6.0, D-56).** The headline is the
    ``(entry, settlement, code)`` claim — did this reader say this *part* of the
    municipality had this institution — in the ``*_settlement`` keys, because
    the settlement is what a birthplace joins to. The ``(entry, code)`` figure
    every earlier report used stays in the unsuffixed keys, unchanged, the same
    unit :func:`compare_inventories` uses.

    Presence ignores counts at both levels: two schools read as one is a
    different and much smaller error than a school read as a chapel, and pooling
    them would let the second hide inside the first. The printed count is scored
    beside it (``count_exact``, ``f1_count``; see :func:`_settlement_scores`).

    Returns one row per pass, sorted best first on the settlement F1.
    ``entries_missed`` is the
    transcriber's entries the pass never reached — excluded from precision and
    recall, and reported so that a pass cannot buy accuracy by reading less.

    ``entry_exact`` is the share of shared entries whose whole claim set matches
    the reference's. F1 pools claims across entries, so it rises when a pass
    moves claims around without finishing a single municipality — and a
    municipality is the unit of analysis downstream, where a settlement either
    has its institutions right or does not. A run whose F1 improves while
    ``entry_exact`` does not has not got closer to a usable page.
    """
    if reference not in passes:
        return []
    ref_entries, ref_claims = _claims(passes[reference])
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for label, records in passes.items():
        if label == reference:
            continue
        entries, claims = _claims(records)
        shared = ref_entries & entries
        mine = {c for c in claims if c[:3] in shared}
        theirs = {c for c in ref_claims if c[:3] in shared}
        hit = mine & theirs
        precision = len(hit) / len(mine) if mine else 0.0
        recall = len(hit) / len(theirs) if theirs else 0.0
        by_entry: dict[tuple, set] = {e: set() for e in shared}
        for claim in mine:
            by_entry[claim[:3]].add(claim[3])
        ref_by_entry: dict[tuple, set] = {e: set() for e in shared}
        for claim in theirs:
            ref_by_entry[claim[:3]].add(claim[3])
        exact = sum(1 for e in shared if by_entry[e] == ref_by_entry[e])
        rows.append({
            "check": "I14_accuracy", "pass": label, "reference": reference,
            "entries_shared": len(shared),
            "entries_missed": len(ref_entries - entries),
            "reference_claims": len(theirs), "claims": len(mine),
            "hit": len(hit), "false": len(mine - theirs),
            "missed": len(theirs - mine),
            "entries_exact": exact,
            "entry_exact": round(exact / len(shared), 3) if shared else 0.0,
            "precision": round(precision, 3), "recall": round(recall, 3),
            "f1": round(2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall), 3)
                  if precision + recall else 0.0,
            **_settlement_scores(passes[reference], records),
        })
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (-r["f1_settlement"], -r["f1"], r["pass"]))


def lexikon_1910_accuracy_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`score_against_reference`."""
    lines = ["lexikon_1910_institutions v" + __version__ + " — I14, accuracy "
             "against the transcription", ""]
    if not rows:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  no reference pass — nothing to score "
                                  "against"])
    lines.append(f"  reference: {rows[0]['reference']}   "
                 f"(each pass scored on the entries it and the reference "
                 f"both read)")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"  {'':22s} {'':5s} {'':5s} "
                 f"{'— settlement (entry, part, symbol) —':^49s} "
                 f"{'— count —':^13s} {'— municipality —':^20s}")
    lines.append(f"  {'pass':22s} {'entr':>5s} {'miss':>5s} {'hit':>5s} "
                 f"{'false':>6s} {'lost':>5s} {'misf':>5s} {'prec':>6s} "
                 f"{'rec':>6s} {'F1':>6s} {'exact':>6s} {'F1':>6s} "
                 f"{'F1':>6s} {'ent.ex':>6s}")
    for row in rows:
        lines.append(f"  {row['pass']:22s} {row['entries_shared']:5d} "
                     f"{row['entries_missed']:5d} {row['hit_settlement']:5d} "
                     f"{row['false_settlement']:6d} "
                     f"{row['missed_settlement']:5d} "
                     f"{row['false_misfiled']:5d} "
                     f"{row['precision_settlement']:6.3f} "
                     f"{row['recall_settlement']:6.3f} "
                     f"{row['f1_settlement']:6.3f} {row['count_exact']:6.3f} "
                     f"{row['f1_count']:6.3f} {row['f1']:6.3f} "
                     f"{row['entry_exact']:6.3f}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("  entr = entries both read (the denominator);  miss = the "
                 "reference's entries")
    lines.append("  this pass never reached — a coverage failure, not a naming "
                 "one, and kept")
    lines.append("  out of the rates so that reading less cannot raise them.")
    lines.append("  settlement = the claim keyed on the PART it is filed under, "
                 "the unit a")
    lines.append("  birthplace joins to. misf = false claims that name an "
                 "institution the")
    lines.append("  municipality does have, under the wrong part "
                 "(part_attribution lists them).")
    lines.append("  count exact = share of hits whose printed count matches; "
                 "count F1 weights")
    lines.append("  each claim by its count. municipality = the pre-2026-09-22 "
                 "unit, for")
    lines.append("  comparison only; ent.ex (whole entry exactly right) is no "
                 "longer a headline.")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def symbol_confusion(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], label: str,
                     reference: str = "human") -> list[dict]:
    """Per-symbol counts, one pass against the reference, on entries both read.

    An F1 is a summary and hides its own shape. Whether a reader is uniformly
    blurry or is missing two specific glyphs decides what to do next, and only
    this shows which: a symbol the reference claims 41 times and the reader
    claims 9 is one pictogram to settle, not a model to replace.
    """
    if reference not in passes or label not in passes:
        return []
    ref_entries, ref_claims = _claims(passes[reference])
    entries, claims = _claims(passes[label])
    shared = ref_entries & entries
    english = {}
    for records in (passes[reference], passes[label]):
        for row in records:
            code = str(row.get("code", "") or "")
            if code.startswith("[") and row.get("english"):
                english.setdefault(code, row["english"])
    codes = {c[3] for c in ref_claims | claims if c[:3] in shared}
    rows = []
    for code in codes:
        in_ref = sum(1 for c in ref_claims if c[:3] in shared and c[3] == code)
        in_pass = sum(1 for c in claims if c[:3] in shared and c[3] == code)
        rows.append({"check": "I15_symbol_error", "pass": label,
                     "reference": reference, "code": code,
                     "english": english.get(code, ""),
                     "reference_claims": in_ref, "pass_claims": in_pass,
                     "delta": in_pass - in_ref})
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (-abs(r["delta"]),
                                       -r["reference_claims"]))


def lexikon_1910_symbol_error_report(rows: list[dict], top: int = 15) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`symbol_confusion` — the glyphs worth a human's time."""
    if not rows:
        return "  nothing to compare"
    lines = [f"  {rows[0]['pass']} vs {rows[0]['reference']}, symbol by symbol "
             f"(entries both read)", ""]
    lines.append(f"  {'symbol':20s} {'reference':>9s} {'pass':>6s} "
                 f"{'delta':>6s}")
    for row in rows[:top]:
        lines.append(f"  {row['code']:20s} {row['reference_claims']:9d} "
                     f"{row['pass_claims']:6d} {row['delta']:+6d}")
    agreed = [r for r in rows if r["delta"] == 0]
    if agreed:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"  exact on {len(agreed)} of {len(rows)} symbols: "
                     + ", ".join(r["code"] for r in agreed[:8])
                     + ("…" if len(agreed) > 8 else ""))
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Three views the settlement figure needs beside it (0.6.0, D-56).
#
# An F1 at the analysis unit says how good the reader is and nothing about
# whether a regression can use what it read. That takes an error rate **per
# institution** (a school dummy and a castle dummy are separate regressors with
# separate misclassification), an interval that respects the fact that entries
# on one page share a scan, a district and a crop, and — while the settlement
# figure sits below the municipality one — a list of the claims that are right
# about the institution and wrong about the part.


def symbol_rates(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], label: str,
                 reference: str = "human", level: str = "settlement",
                 units: set | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Sensitivity and specificity of one pass, glyph by glyph.

    For each symbol, every unit on the entries both sides read is one of
    ``tp`` (both claim it), ``fp`` (only the pass), ``fn`` (only the reference)
    or ``tn`` (neither). ``sensitivity = tp / (tp + fn)`` and
    ``specificity = tn / (tn + fp)``; either is **blank**, not zero, where its
    denominator is empty — a glyph the reference never prints has no measured
    sensitivity.

    ``units`` is the universe of units, as ``entry + (part,)`` tuples (or bare
    entries at ``municipality`` level). Left out, it is every unit either
    inventory has a row for — and an inventory only has rows where something
    was printed or read, so a part with no institutions at all is missing from
    it. Those are true negatives for every glyph, so the default **understates
    specificity**; pass the parts read from the gold sheets to close that.
    """
    if reference not in passes or label not in passes:
        return []
    _shared, seen, theirs, mine = _shared_claims(passes[reference],
                                                 passes[label], level)
    shared_entries = {c[:3] for c in seen}
    universe = {c[:-1] for c in theirs.keys() | mine.keys()}
    universe |= ({u for u in units if u[:3] in shared_entries}
                 if units is not None else seen)
    rows = []
    for code in sorted({c[-1] for c in theirs.keys() | mine.keys()}):
        in_ref = {c for c in theirs if c[-1] == code}
        in_pass = {c for c in mine if c[-1] == code}
        tp, fp, fn = (len(in_ref & in_pass), len(in_pass - in_ref),
                      len(in_ref - in_pass))
        tn = len(universe) - tp - fp - fn
        rows.append({"check": "I16_symbol_rates", "pass": label,
                     "reference": reference, "level": level, "code": code,
                     "units": len(universe), "tp": tp, "fp": fp, "fn": fn,
                     "tn": tn,
                     "sensitivity": round(tp / (tp + fn), 3) if tp + fn else "",
                     "specificity": round(tn / (tn + fp), 3) if tn + fp else ""})
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (-(r["fp"] + r["fn"]), r["code"]))


def lexikon_1910_symbol_rates_report(rows: list[dict], top: int = 20) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`symbol_rates`."""
    if not rows:
        return "  nothing to compare"
    first = rows[0]
    lines = [f"  {first['pass']} vs {first['reference']}, per glyph at "
             f"{first['level']} level — {first['units']} units on entries "
             f"both read", ""]
    lines.append(f"  {'symbol':22s} {'tp':>4s} {'fp':>4s} {'fn':>4s} {'tn':>5s} "
                 f"{'sens':>6s} {'spec':>6s}")
    show = lambda value: f"{value:6.3f}" if value != "" else f"{'':6s}"
    for row in rows[:top]:
        lines.append(f"  {row['code']:22s} {row['tp']:4d} {row['fp']:4d} "
                     f"{row['fn']:4d} {row['tn']:5d} {show(row['sensitivity'])} "
                     f"{show(row['specificity'])}")
    clean = [r for r in rows if not r["fp"] and not r["fn"]]
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"  no error on {len(clean)} of {len(rows)} glyphs.  A blank "
                 f"rate has an empty denominator.")
    lines.append("  Units are those either inventory has a row for; a part "
                 "with nothing printed")
    lines.append("  is absent, so specificity is understated unless `units` "
                 "is supplied.")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _misfiling_kind(want: set, got: set) -> str:
    """How the pass's parts for one institution differ from the reference's."""
    if want == {WHOLE} and WHOLE not in got:
        return "whole_to_part"      # municipality-wide, filed under a part
    if got == {WHOLE} and WHOLE not in want:
        return "part_to_whole"      # a part's institution, filed on the whole
    if got < want:
        return "part_missed"        # right parts, not all of them
    if got > want:
        return "part_added"         # every right part, and one more
    return "part_shifted"


def part_attribution(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], label: str,
                     reference: str = "human") -> list[dict]:
    """Institutions the pass names correctly and files under the wrong part.

    One row per ``(entry, code)`` that both sides claim for the municipality but
    on different parts. This is the whole of the gap between the municipality
    and settlement figures, itemised: the decoder's ``— n)`` continuation was
    its largest term (fixed in 0.5.0), and what is left has not been diagnosed.
    ``kind`` sorts the rows so the residue can be read as a pattern rather than
    a list — see :func:`_misfiling_kind`.
    """
    if reference not in passes or label not in passes:
        return []
    _shared, _units, theirs, mine = _shared_claims(passes[reference],
                                                   passes[label], "settlement")

    def parts(claims) -> dict[tuple, set]:
        out: dict[tuple, set] = {}
        for claim in claims:
            out.setdefault(claim[:3] + (claim[-1],), set()).add(claim[3])
        return out

    ref_parts, my_parts = parts(theirs), parts(mine)
    rows = []
    for key in sorted(ref_parts.keys() & my_parts.keys(),
                      key=lambda k: tuple(map(str, k))):
        want, got = ref_parts[key], my_parts[key]
        if want == got:
            continue
        page, district, muni_seq, code = key
        rows.append({"check": "I17_part_attribution", "pass": label,
                     "reference": reference, "page": page,
                     "district": district, "muni_seq": muni_seq, "code": code,
                     "reference_parts": " ".join(sorted(want)),
                     "pass_parts": " ".join(sorted(got)),
                     "kind": _misfiling_kind(want, got)})
    return rows


def lexikon_1910_part_attribution_report(rows: list[dict], top: int = 10) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`part_attribution`."""
    if not rows:
        return "  every institution both sides name is filed under the same parts"
    lines = [f"  {rows[0]['pass']} vs {rows[0]['reference']}: {len(rows)} "
             f"institutions named correctly and filed under the wrong part", ""]

    def tally(key) -> list[tuple]:
        counts: dict = {}
        for row in rows:
            counts[key(row)] = counts.get(key(row), 0) + 1
        return sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], str(kv[0])))

    for title, key in (
            ("by kind", lambda r: r["kind"]),
            ("by page", lambda r: r["page"]),
            ("by parts, reference -> pass",
             lambda r: f"{r['reference_parts']} -> {r['pass_parts']}"),
            ("by symbol", lambda r: r["code"])):
        lines.append(f"  {title}:")
        for value, n in tally(key)[:top]:
            lines.append(f"    {n:4d}x  {value}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def clustered_interval(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], label: str,
                       reference: str = "human", level: str = "settlement",
                       draws: int = 2000,
                       seed: int = BOOTSTRAP_SEED) -> dict:
    """F1 with a percentile interval from resampling **pages**, not claims.

    Claims on one page share a scan, a print run, a district and the crops the
    reader was shown, so they are one cluster and not that many independent
    draws. Each bootstrap draw picks pages with replacement and pools their hit
    / false / missed counts into one F1.

    ``f1_by_page`` is printed beside the interval because with few pages it is
    the more honest object: ``G`` pages allow few distinct resamples, so the
    percentile interval is coarse and too narrow. ``f1_lo`` and ``f1_hi`` are
    blank with fewer than two pages.
    """
    blank = {"check": "I18_clustered_interval", "pass": label,
             "reference": reference, "level": level, "pages": 0, "draws": draws,
             "f1": "", "f1_lo": "", "f1_hi": "", "f1_by_page": ""}
    if reference not in passes or label not in passes:
        return blank
    _shared, _units, theirs, mine = _shared_claims(passes[reference],
                                                   passes[label], level)
    counts: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
    for claim in theirs.keys() | mine.keys():
        slot = counts.setdefault(str(claim[0]), [0, 0, 0])
        slot[0 if claim in theirs and claim in mine
             else 1 if claim in mine else 2] += 1
    if not counts:
        return blank
    pages = sorted(counts)
    pooled = lambda picked: _prf(*(sum(counts[p][k] for p in picked)
                                   for k in range(3)))[2]
    out = {**blank, "pages": len(pages), "f1": round(pooled(pages), 3),
           "f1_by_page": " ".join(f"{p}={pooled([p]):.3f}" for p in pages)}
    if len(pages) < 2 or draws < 1:
        return out
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    f1s = sorted(pooled([rng.choice(pages) for _ in pages])
                 for _ in range(draws))
    out["f1_lo"] = round(f1s[int(_TAIL * draws)], 3)
    out["f1_hi"] = round(f1s[max(int((1 - _TAIL) * draws) - 1, 0)], 3)
    return out


def lexikon_1910_clustered_interval_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`clustered_interval`, one line per pass."""
    rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("pages")]
    if not rows:
        return "  nothing to compare"
    lines = [f"  F1 at {rows[0]['level']} level, {INTERVAL:.0%} percentile "
             f"interval over pages ({rows[0]['draws']} draws)", ""]
    for row in rows:
        interval = (f"[{row['f1_lo']:.3f}, {row['f1_hi']:.3f}]"
                    if row["f1_lo"] != "" else "[one page: no interval]")
        lines.append(f"  {row['pass']:22s} {row['f1']:.3f} {interval:16s} "
                     f"{row['pages']} pages   {row['f1_by_page']}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("  Pages are the clusters. With this few, the interval is "
                 "coarse and too narrow;")
    lines.append("  the per-page figures beside it are the evidence, the "
                 "interval a summary of them.")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What a second reader is worth to a first.
#
# Accuracy against the transcriber ranks readers one at a time. A SECOND reader
# is not chosen that way: it routes and never overwrites (D-38, D-55), so the
# question is not how often it is right but whether it is wrong somewhere else.
# Two readers at 0.97 that make the same mistakes are one reader, read twice.


def _excess_tail(population: int, marked: int, drawn: int, overlap: int) -> float:
    r"""$P(X \ge \text{overlap})$ for a hypergeometric $X$.

    ``drawn`` items are taken from ``population``, of which ``marked`` are
    special; $X$ counts the special ones drawn:

    $$P(X \ge x) = \sum_{k=x}^{\min(K, n)} \binom{K}{k}\binom{N-K}{n-k} \Big/ \binom{N}{n}$$
    """
    if overlap <= 0 or not population:
        return 1.0
    ways = sum(math.comb(marked, k) * math.comb(population - marked, drawn - k)
               for k in range(overlap, min(marked, drawn) + 1))
    return ways / math.comb(population, drawn)


def second_reader(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], first: str, second: str,
                  reference: str = "human", level: str = "settlement") -> dict:
    """Which of the first reader's errors a second reader would bring to review.

    A claim both readers make, or neither does, is accepted; a claim only one of
    them makes is flagged. So the second reader's own accuracy is not the figure
    that matters — where its errors fall is:

    ``caught``        errors of the first the second disagrees with it on. They
                      reach review.
    ``shared_errors`` errors both make. Nothing in the pair shows them, and they
                      are what is left in the data after a perfect review.
    ``false_alarms``  claims the first has right and the second does not: review
                      load that buys nothing.

    ``f1_after_review`` is the first reader's F1 if every flagged claim were
    settled correctly — the ceiling this pair can reach, not a forecast.

    The ``missed_*`` block is the test D-58 asks for. Given the truth, two
    readers' errors should fall independently; on the claims the reference has,
    the number both miss is then hypergeometric and ``missed_p`` is its upper
    tail (Fisher's exact test, one-sided — the exact form of the permutation
    check). A small ``missed_p`` says the two miss the same claims more often
    than chance would have it: a shared blind spot. **Two cautions.** Claims on
    one page are not independent draws, so the tail is too small rather than too
    large; and with a dozen misses the test has little power, so a large
    ``missed_p`` is not evidence of independence. False claims get no such test —
    it needs the universe of claims that could have been made — and are counts.

    Scored on the entries all three read, at ``level``; presence only.
    """
    blank = {"check": "I21_second_reader", "first": first, "second": second,
             "reference": reference, "level": level, "entries_shared": 0}
    if not all(name in passes for name in (reference, first, second)):
        return blank
    read = [_claim_counts(passes[name], level)
            for name in (reference, first, second)]
    shared = read[0][0] & read[1][0] & read[2][0]
    truth, one, two = ({c for c in claims if c[:3] in shared}
                       for _entries, _units, claims in read)
    errors_one, errors_two, flagged = one ^ truth, two ^ truth, one ^ two
    missed_one, missed_two = truth - one, truth - two
    false_both, missed_both = (one - truth) & (two - truth), missed_one & missed_two
    share = lambda n, d: round(n / d, 3) if d else ""           # noqa: E731
    return {
        **blank, "entries_shared": len(shared), "reference_claims": len(truth),
        "first_errors": len(errors_one), "second_errors": len(errors_two),
        "caught": len(errors_one & flagged),
        "shared_errors": len(errors_one & errors_two),
        "catch_rate": share(len(errors_one & flagged), len(errors_one)),
        "flagged": len(flagged), "false_alarms": len(flagged - errors_one),
        "f1_first": round(_prf(len(one & truth), len(one - truth),
                               len(missed_one))[2], 3),
        "f1_after_review": round(_prf(len(truth) - len(missed_both),
                                      len(false_both), len(missed_both))[2], 3),
        "missed_first": len(missed_one), "missed_second": len(missed_two),
        "missed_both": len(missed_both),
        "missed_both_expected": (round(len(missed_one) * len(missed_two)
                                       / len(truth), 2) if truth else ""),
        "missed_p": round(_excess_tail(len(truth), len(missed_one),
                                       len(missed_two), len(missed_both)), 4),
        "false_first": len(one - truth), "false_second": len(two - truth),
        "false_both": len(false_both),
    }


def lexikon_1910_second_reader_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`second_reader`, one line per pair of readers."""
    rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("entries_shared")]
    if not rows:
        return "  nothing to compare"
    lines = [f"  what a second reader would bring to review — "
             f"{rows[0]['level']} level, against {rows[0]['reference']}", "",
             f"  {'first':22s} {'second':22s} {'errors':>6s} {'caught':>6s} "
             f"{'rate':>6s} {'shared':>6s} {'alarms':>6s} {'F1':>6s} {'F1 after':>8s}"]
    for row in rows:
        rate = f"{row['catch_rate']:.3f}" if row["catch_rate"] != "" else "—"
        lines.append(
            f"  {row['first']:22s} {row['second']:22s} {row['first_errors']:6d} "
            f"{row['caught']:6d} {rate:>6s} {row['shared_errors']:6d} "
            f"{row['false_alarms']:6d} {row['f1_first']:6.3f} "
            f"{row['f1_after_review']:8.3f}")
    lines += ["", "  claims the reference has that both readers miss — observed, "
                  "expected if their", "  misses fell independently, and the chance "
                  "of that many or more (D-58):", ""]
    for row in rows:
        chance = (f"p = {row['missed_p']:.4f}" if row["missed_p"] >= 0.0001
                  else "p < 0.0001")
        lines.append(
            f"  {row['first']:22s} {row['second']:22s} "
            f"{row['missed_first']:3d} and {row['missed_second']:3d} of "
            f"{row['reference_claims']}: both {row['missed_both']:3d}, expected "
            f"{row['missed_both_expected']}, {chance}   "
            f"false: {row['false_first']} and {row['false_second']}, "
            f"both {row['false_both']}")
    lines += ["", "  `caught` reaches review; `shared` is what a perfect review "
                  "still leaves; `alarms`",
              "  is review load on claims the first reader had right. A small p "
              "is a shared blind",
              "  spot. A large one is not independence: with this few misses "
              "the test is weak."]
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# I22 — the printed order of the marks.
#
# The marks of one part are set in a fixed order, and the volume says so by
# example: its Návod (p. VIII) reads Bílina's entry out in full — offices and
# courts, the revenue marks, gendarmes and transport station, the churches, the
# schools, kindergarten, welfare, hospital, pharmacy, doctors, vet, midwives,
# fire brigade; savings bank, the cooperative and its letters; post, telegraph,
# telephone, railway; and, on the pages, castle and ruin last. A mark that sits
# where the print never sets it is therefore evidence — about the mark, or about
# where the part was cut.
#
# The order is not typed in from the Návod. It is LEARNED, as pairwise
# precedence, from the transcribed gold sheets (purposive and calibration; see
# `read_transcription_md.read_order_reference`), because one worked example
# names a third of the atlas and the sheets show the rest. A pair the sheets
# never show together is not judged at all.
#
# Like every stage here it ROUTES and never overwrites (D-38, D-55): the
# functions below return which marks to look at and change no record.

#: The marks with two printed positions, never judged. At a court seat or beside
#: state authorities they follow the offices (Bílina: ``… o. nemoc. pokl.,
#: 5 [gendarme], [transport-station], arcid. …``); elsewhere they follow the fire
#: brigade. Measured 2026-10-13 on the ten transcribed sheets: every one of the
#: 72 pair observations that run against the majority direction involves one of
#: these three, and none of the 2,902 that do not.
ORDER_FLOATING = frozenset({"[gendarme]", "[canteen]", "[transport-station]"})

#: How often the reference must print a pair one way — and never the other —
#: before the other way counts as reversed. Two, not one: a pair seen once rests
#: on a single line of a single sheet, and one slip of the transcriber's would
#: become a rule. The four scored pages do not decide it. Measured 2026-10-13 on
#: the nine stored `r4` passes of gemini38, gemini37 and haiku55nh, each page
#: judged on the others: false claims flagged a pass 1–5 at one sighting (2 in
#: five of the six Gemini passes), 1–5 at two (1 in all six) and the same at
#: three; true claims flagged 0–1 at one and at two, 0 at three.
ORDER_MIN_SEEN = 2

#: Marks that must be out of place before an order that divides cleanly in two
#: is called a restart. With one, a misread mark at the end of the line and a
#: one-mark part run on from below are the same picture, and the mark is what is
#: reported.
ORDER_RESTART_MIN = 2

#: Above this many marks out of place the smallest set is not searched for
#: exactly (the search doubles with each mark) and the greedy set is returned.
#: A part that far out of order is a parsing question whichever marks are named.
ORDER_EXACT_LIMIT = 12

VERDICT_OUT_OF_PLACE = "out_of_place"
VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS = "order_restarts"

#: Text the print sets in parentheses: a post office's name, a school's
#: language note. Blanked, not deleted, so positions stay true to the entry.
_ORDER_PAREN_RE = re.compile(r"\([^()]*\)")

#: A named part inside an entry — ``Kartouzy: … . Valdice: [school] III`` — a
#: capitalised name and a colon after a stop or at the start. The order begins
#: again there. Never the ``[cooperative]:`` list, which opens with a bracket.
_ORDER_NAMED_PART_RE = re.compile(r"(?:(?<=[.;,])|^)\s*[A-ZÁ-Ž][\w\- ]{2,40}:\s")

#: The same prefix as far as a stored record shows it: its ``context`` window
#: ends, just before the mark, in a letter, a colon and at most a count.
_ORDER_NAMED_BEFORE_RE = re.compile(r"[a-zá-ž]:\s*(?:\d+\s*)?$")


def _order_code(record: dict) -> str:
    """The record's code if it is a mark the order is learned on, else ``""``.

    Bracketed symbols only. An abbreviation is decoded out of running words
    (``šk.`` inside ``o. šk. rada``), and where a word falls is not where a mark
    is set.
    """
    code = str(record.get("code", "") or "")
    return code if _SYMBOL_CODE_RE.match(code) and code != UNPLACED else ""


def order_runs(records: list[dict], text: str | None = None) -> list[list[dict]]:
    """One entry's symbol records, in printed order, cut where the order restarts.

    ``records`` are :func:`decode_entry`'s for **one** entry — one numbered part,
    which is where the order restarts anyway. They are sorted by ``position``
    and cut again at each named part (``Valdice:``). Returns the runs, each a
    list of the records themselves; runs with no symbol are left out.

    With the entry's ``text`` the cut is :data:`_ORDER_NAMED_PART_RE` and a mark
    inside parentheses is dropped. Without it — a pass stored as
    ``institutions_<label>.csv`` keeps the records and not the text — the cut is
    read off each record's ``context``.

    **Blind to, without the text:** a named part whose first words are not a
    mark (``Kartouzy: věznice …, [doctor]``), because the name is then outside
    the mark's window; and parentheses, so a mark the reader wrote inside them
    is judged with the rest.
    """
    marks = sorted((r for r in records if _order_code(r)),
                   key=lambda r: int(r.get("position") or 0))
    if text is None:
        runs: list[list[dict]] = []
        for record in marks:
            context = str(record.get("context", "") or "")
            before = context[:max(context.find(record["code"]), 0)]
            if not runs or _ORDER_NAMED_BEFORE_RE.search(before):
                runs.append([])
            runs[-1].append(record)
        return runs
    spans = [m.span() for m in _ORDER_PAREN_RE.finditer(text)]
    blanked = _ORDER_PAREN_RE.sub(lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), text)
    cuts = [m.end() for m in _ORDER_NAMED_PART_RE.finditer(blanked)]
    by_part: dict[int, list[dict]] = {}
    for record in marks:
        position = int(record.get("position") or 0)
        if any(start <= position < end for start, end in spans):
            continue
        by_part.setdefault(sum(1 for cut in cuts if cut <= position),
                           []).append(record)
    return [by_part[part] for part in sorted(by_part)]


def learn_order(reference: list[dict], leave_out_page: str = "") -> dict:
    """``{(a, b): n}`` — how often the reference prints mark ``a`` before ``b``.

    ``reference`` is one row per run, ``{"page": …, "codes": [...]}``, as
    ``read_transcription_md.read_order_reference`` returns it. Every pair of
    positions holding two different marks counts once, adjacent or not.

    ``leave_out_page`` drops one page's runs. Use it when the result will judge
    a reading of that same page: the page's own gold would otherwise vouch for
    whatever order the reader copied off it, right or wrong.

    **Blind to:** anything about a pair the reference never prints together —
    it is absent from the result, and absent is "not judged", never "allowed".
    """
    before: dict[tuple, int] = {}
    for row in reference:
        if leave_out_page and str(row.get("page", "")) == str(leave_out_page):
            continue
        codes = row["codes"]
        for i in range(len(codes)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(codes)):
                if codes[i] != codes[j]:
                    pair = (codes[i], codes[j])
                    before[pair] = before.get(pair, 0) + 1
    return before


def _reversed_pairs(codes: list[str], order: dict,
                    min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """``(i, j)`` for each pair of positions the reference only prints the other way.

    Reversed means: seen ``b`` before ``a`` at least ``min_seen`` times, and
    ``a`` before ``b`` never. :data:`ORDER_FLOATING` is on neither side of any
    pair.
    """
    pairs = []
    for i in range(len(codes)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(codes)):
            a, b = codes[i], codes[j]
            if a == b or a in ORDER_FLOATING or b in ORDER_FLOATING:
                continue
            if order.get((b, a), 0) >= min_seen and not order.get((a, b), 0):
                pairs.append((i, j))
    return pairs


def _covers(pairs: list[tuple[int, int]], budget: int):
    """Every way to touch all ``pairs`` with at most ``budget`` positions."""
    if not pairs:
        yield frozenset()
        return
    if budget:
        for pick in pairs[0]:
            rest = [pair for pair in pairs if pick not in pair]
            for cover in _covers(rest, budget - 1):
                yield cover | {pick}


def _greedy_cover(pairs: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[int]:
    """Take the position in most pairs, the later on a tie, until none is left."""
    left, taken = list(pairs), []
    while left:
        load: dict[int, int] = {}
        for pair in left:
            for position in pair:
                load[position] = load.get(position, 0) + 1
        worst = max(load, key=lambda position: (load[position], position))
        taken.append(worst)
        left = [pair for pair in left if worst not in pair]
    return sorted(taken)


def _smallest_cover(pairs: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[int]:
    """The fewest positions that touch every pair; of several, the latest printed."""
    greedy = _greedy_cover(pairs)
    for size in range(min(len(greedy), ORDER_EXACT_LIMIT) + 1):
        found = set(_covers(pairs, size))
        if found:
            return sorted(max(found, key=lambda c: sorted(c, reverse=True)))
    return greedy


def out_of_order(codes: list[str], order: dict,
                 min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> list[int]:
    """Positions of the fewest marks whose removal leaves no reversed pair.

    ``codes`` is one run's marks in printed order (:func:`order_runs`),
    ``order`` is :func:`learn_order`'s. A castle read as a poorhouse at the end
    of a line stands after the post, the telegraph and the station, all of
    which the print sets after a poorhouse — several reversed pairs, one mark
    in all of them, and that mark is the answer. Empty when nothing is reversed.

    **Blind to:**

    * a **same-slot substitution** — station for stop, revenue office for
      customs, one church for another, a savings bank written straight before
      the cooperative. The wrong mark stands where the right one would, so no
      pair is reversed. Most of what the readers still get wrong is this;
    * **which of two** — one reversed pair between two marks says one of them is
      wrong, not which. The later one is returned; the caller shows both;
    * a **missing** mark, which reverses nothing;
    * the three marks of :data:`ORDER_FLOATING`, wherever they stand;
    * a pair the reference shows fewer than ``min_seen`` times. The reference is
      ten pages of one edition, the Czech one.
    """
    return _smallest_cover(_reversed_pairs(codes, order, min_seen))


def order_restart(codes: list[str], order: dict,
                  min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> int | None:
    """Where the order begins again inside one run, or ``None``.

    The second verdict. If every reversed pair runs across one point — the marks
    before it in order among themselves, the marks from it on in order among
    themselves, and only the two groups out of order with each other — the
    marks are not misread, the run is two: a part or an entry boundary was
    missed (``— 2)`` lost, two printed lines joined, a named part's colon
    dropped). That is a **parsing question**, and it is reported as one.

    Returns the position of the first mark of the second group, which is the
    first mark that belongs before something printed earlier. A mark between
    the two groups that is reversed with nothing could sit on either side.

    **Blind to:** a second part too short to show —
    :data:`ORDER_RESTART_MIN` marks must be out of place, so a one-mark part run
    on from below, or one whose only reversed mark is its first, comes back from
    :func:`out_of_order` as that mark; a second part that only repeats marks
    of the first (``[school] … — 2) [school]``), because a mark is never
    reversed with itself; and the reverse error — two neighbouring marks both
    misread as marks that belong earlier (the gendarme and canteen after a fire
    brigade read as ``[customs]``, ``[gauging]``) divide the line the same way
    and are called a restart too.
    """
    pairs = _reversed_pairs(codes, order, min_seen)
    if not pairs:
        return None
    cut = min(j for _i, j in pairs)
    if max(i for i, _j in pairs) >= cut:
        return None
    return cut if len(_smallest_cover(pairs)) >= ORDER_RESTART_MIN else None


def _order_entry(record: dict) -> tuple:
    """One printed part, as the decoder cut it: the unit a run is taken from."""
    return (str(record.get("page", "")), str(record.get("district", "")),
            str(record.get("muni_seq", "")), str(record.get("settlement_seq", "")),
            str(record.get("entry_index", "")))


def check_order(records: list[dict], reference: list[dict],
                texts: dict | None = None, leave_page_out: bool = False,
                min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> list[dict]:
    """One row per mark the printed order sends to review. Changes no record.

    ``records`` are decoded records of any number of entries
    (:func:`decode_sections`, or a stored ``institutions_<label>.csv``);
    ``reference`` is what :func:`learn_order` takes. ``texts`` maps
    ``(page, district, entry_index)`` to the entry's text where the caller has
    it. ``leave_page_out`` learns the order afresh for each page from the other
    pages — required when the records are readings of the reference's own
    pages, which is the case whenever this is scored.

    ``verdict`` is :data:`VERDICT_OUT_OF_PLACE` (look at this mark) or
    :data:`VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS` (look at where this part was cut; the rows
    are then the marks :func:`out_of_order` names, and ``restart_code`` is the
    first mark of the second group). ``against`` lists the marks each one is
    reversed with, ``sequence`` the whole run as read.
    """
    by_entry: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    for record in records:
        by_entry.setdefault(_order_entry(record), []).append(record)
    orders: dict[str, dict] = {}
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for entry, mine in by_entry.items():
        page = entry[0] if leave_page_out else ""
        if page not in orders:
            orders[page] = learn_order(reference, leave_out_page=page)
        text = (texts or {}).get((entry[0], entry[1], entry[4]))
        for named_part, run in enumerate(order_runs(mine, text)):
            codes = [record["code"] for record in run]
            pairs = _reversed_pairs(codes, orders[page], min_seen)
            if not pairs:
                continue
            restart = order_restart(codes, orders[page], min_seen)
            for position in _smallest_cover(pairs):
                against = [codes[j if i == position else i]
                           for i, j in pairs if position in (i, j)]
                rows.append({
                    "check": "I22_order", "page": entry[0], "district": entry[1],
                    "muni_seq": entry[2], "settlement_seq": entry[3],
                    "entry_index": entry[4], "named_part": named_part,
                    "code": codes[position],
                    "position": run[position].get("position", ""),
                    "verdict": (VERDICT_OUT_OF_PLACE if restart is None
                                else VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS),
                    "against": " ".join(dict.fromkeys(against)),
                    "restart_code": "" if restart is None else codes[restart],
                    "sequence": " ".join(codes)})
    return rows


def order_summary(reference: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """What the reference order rests on, counted from its rows rather than typed.

    ``against_majority`` counts pair observations that run the less common way
    for their pair; ``*_fixed`` is the same with :data:`ORDER_FLOATING` left
    out, and is the figure the check stands on.
    """
    order = learn_order(reference)
    pairs = {tuple(sorted(pair)) for pair in order}
    fixed = [p for p in pairs if not set(p) & ORDER_FLOATING]
    seen = lambda p: (order.get(p, 0), order.get(p[::-1], 0))   # noqa: E731
    count = lambda some: sum(sum(seen(p)) for p in some)        # noqa: E731
    minority = lambda some: sum(min(seen(p)) for p in some)     # noqa: E731
    return {"pages": len({str(row.get("page", "")) for row in reference}),
            "runs": len(reference),
            "marks": sum(len(row["codes"]) for row in reference),
            "pairs": len(pairs), "observations": count(pairs),
            "against_majority": minority(pairs),
            "pairs_fixed": len(fixed), "observations_fixed": count(fixed),
            "against_majority_fixed": minority(fixed)}


def order_reference_flags(reference: list[dict],
                          min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> list[dict]:
    """The reference's own runs that the other pages' order would flag.

    Each page is judged on the order learned without it. A row here is a line
    of a gold sheet to look at again — a slip of the transcriber's, or a place
    where the print departs from its own order. It is reported and nothing is
    changed: the sheets are the author's to rule on.
    """
    rows = []
    for run in reference:
        order = learn_order(reference, leave_out_page=run.get("page", ""))
        codes = run["codes"]
        marks = out_of_order(codes, order, min_seen)
        if marks:
            restart = order_restart(codes, order, min_seen)
            rows.append({**{k: v for k, v in run.items() if k != "codes"},
                         "verdict": (VERDICT_OUT_OF_PLACE if restart is None
                                     else VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS),
                         "marks": " ".join(codes[i] for i in marks),
                         "sequence": " ".join(codes)})
    return rows


def order_joins(reference: list[dict], min_seen: int = ORDER_MIN_SEEN) -> dict:
    """Would the order have shown a missed boundary? Simulated on the reference.

    Each two runs printed one after the other in the same municipality — two
    numbered parts, or two named parts of one — are run together, as a decoder
    that missed the boundary would leave them, and judged on the order learned
    without their page. ``shown`` is how many joins leave any mark out of place;
    ``restarts`` how many of those get the parsing verdict of
    :func:`order_restart`. ``one_mark`` counts the joins whose shorter side is a
    single mark, which can never be called a restart.

    A power check on the check, not a property of any reader.
    """
    out = {"joins": 0, "shown": 0, "restarts": 0, "one_mark": 0}
    municipality = lambda row: (row.get("page"), row.get("district"),   # noqa: E731
                                row.get("muni_seq"))
    for above, below in zip(reference, reference[1:]):
        if municipality(above) != municipality(below):
            continue
        order = learn_order(reference, leave_out_page=above.get("page", ""))
        joined = above["codes"] + below["codes"]
        out["joins"] += 1
        out["one_mark"] += min(len(above["codes"]), len(below["codes"])) == 1
        out["shown"] += bool(out_of_order(joined, order, min_seen))
        out["restarts"] += order_restart(joined, order, min_seen) is not None
    return out


def order_sheet_rows(reference: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """The order reference's runs as inventory rows, one per mark.

    What the gold sheets print in each part, in the shape :func:`_claim_counts`
    keys a claim on — so a flag on a page outside the scored gold can still be
    held against the sheet's own line for that part.
    """
    return [{"page": run.get("page", ""), "district": run.get("district", ""),
             "muni_seq": str(run.get("muni_seq", "")),
             "settlement_seq": str(run.get("settlement_seq", "")), "code": code}
            for run in reference for code in run["codes"]]


def order_scores(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], flags: dict[str, list[dict]],
                 reference: str = "human", level: str = "settlement",
                 sheets: list[dict] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """What the order check flags in each pass, against the reference's truth.

    ``passes`` are inventories, the reference among them; ``flags`` maps a
    label to its :func:`check_order` rows. Scored as the accuracy table is: on
    the entries the pass and the reference both read, at ``level``, presence
    only. A claim is flagged when any mark carrying it is.

    ``false_flagged`` is the check doing its work; ``true_flagged`` is review
    load on claims that were right. ``restart_parts`` counts the parts given
    the parsing verdict, on any page.

    ``flagged_elsewhere`` counts flagged claims on entries the reference does
    not cover. With ``sheets`` — the order reference's own runs — those are
    held against the sheet's line for the part: ``elsewhere_on_sheets`` are on
    a part some sheet transcribes, ``elsewhere_absent`` are marks that sheet
    does not print there. **These two are weaker evidence than the scored
    columns:** the sheets outside the scored gold are single-coded and partly
    still drafts, and they are the sheets the order was learned from (each
    page is judged on the others, so no line vouches for itself).
    """
    sheet_units, sheet_claims = set(), {}
    if sheets:
        _entries, sheet_units, sheet_claims = _claim_counts(
            order_sheet_rows(sheets), level)
    rows = []
    for label, records in passes.items():
        if label == reference or label not in flags:
            continue
        shared, _units, theirs, mine = _shared_claims(passes[reference], records,
                                                      level)
        flagged = set(_claim_counts(flags[label], level)[2])
        false, true = mine.keys() - theirs.keys(), mine.keys() & theirs.keys()
        elsewhere = {c for c in flagged if c[:3] not in shared}
        on_sheets = {c for c in elsewhere if c[:-1] in sheet_units}
        rows.append({
            "check": "I22_order", "pass": label, "reference": reference,
            "level": level, "false": len(false),
            "false_flagged": len(false & flagged), "true": len(true),
            "true_flagged": len(true & flagged),
            "flagged_elsewhere": len(elsewhere),
            "elsewhere_on_sheets": len(on_sheets),
            "elsewhere_absent": len(on_sheets - sheet_claims.keys()),
            "restart_parts": len({_order_entry(row) + (row["named_part"],)
                                  for row in flags[label]
                                  if row["verdict"] == VERDICT_ORDER_RESTARTS})})
    return rows


def order_disputes(passes: dict[str, list[dict]], flags: dict[str, list[dict]],
                   first: str, second: str, reference: str = "human",
                   level: str = "settlement") -> dict:
    """What the order says about the claims two readers disagree on.

    A disputed claim is one only one of the two makes, on the entries both and
    the reference read — the claims :func:`second_reader` sends to review. The
    order check can speak on such a claim only through the reader that made
    it: ``flagged`` counts the disputed claims whose maker's reading it flags,
    ``flagged_false`` those of them the reference does not have (the flag
    points at the wrong side of the dispute, correctly), ``flagged_true`` those
    it does (the flag is wrong). The ``first_*`` and ``second_*`` keys split
    the same counts by who made the claim.

    ``agreed_false`` are the false claims **both** make — accepted by the pair
    unseen, since nothing is disputed — and ``agreed_false_flagged`` those of
    them a mark out of place carries in either reading. The order does not
    depend on the two readers disagreeing, so it can reach these.

    It routes: a flag is a reason to look at that reader's mark first, and
    settles nothing by itself.

    **Blind to:** a disputed claim that is *missing* from one reader. Its
    absence reverses no pair, so the check is silent on the reader that
    dropped it and can only ever speak against the one that wrote it.
    """
    blank = {"check": "I22_order", "first": first, "second": second,
             "reference": reference, "level": level, "disputed": 0}
    names = (reference, first, second)
    if not all(name in passes for name in names) or not all(
            name in flags for name in (first, second)):
        return blank
    read = [_claim_counts(passes[name], level) for name in names]
    shared = read[0][0] & read[1][0] & read[2][0]
    truth, one, two = ({c for c in claims if c[:3] in shared}
                       for _entries, _units, claims in read)
    marked = {name: set(_claim_counts(flags[name], level)[2])
              for name in (first, second)}
    agreed_false = (one & two) - truth
    out = {**blank, "disputed": len(one ^ two),
           "disputed_false": len((one ^ two) - truth),
           "agreed_false": len(agreed_false),
           "agreed_false_flagged": len(agreed_false
                                       & (marked[first] | marked[second]))}
    total = {"flagged": 0, "flagged_false": 0, "flagged_true": 0}
    for who, made, name in (("first", one - two, first),
                            ("second", two - one, second)):
        flagged = made & marked[name]
        mine = {"flagged": len(flagged), "flagged_false": len(flagged - truth),
                "flagged_true": len(flagged & truth)}
        out.update({f"{who}_disputed": len(made),
                    f"{who}_disputed_false": len(made - truth),
                    **{f"{who}_{key}": n for key, n in mine.items()}})
        total = {key: total[key] + n for key, n in mine.items()}
    return {**out, **total}


def lexikon_1910_order_report(summary: dict, scores: list[dict],
                              sheet_flags: list[dict] | None = None,
                              joins: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """Ledger for I22: the reference, then each pass (:func:`order_scores`)."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_institutions v{__version__} — I22, the printed order "
             f"of the marks", "",
             f"  reference order: {summary['runs']} runs of marks on "
             f"{summary['pages']} gold pages, {summary['marks']} symbols, "
             f"{summary['pairs']} pairs seen together",
             f"  pair observations {summary['observations']}, "
             f"{summary['against_majority']} against the majority direction; "
             f"without {', '.join(sorted(ORDER_FLOATING))}:",
             f"  {summary['observations_fixed']} observations of "
             f"{summary['pairs_fixed']} pairs, "
             f"{summary['against_majority_fixed']} against the majority"]
    if joins:
        lines += ["", f"  two adjacent parts run together, simulated on the "
                      f"reference: {joins['shown']} of {joins['joins']} joins "
                      f"leave a mark out of place,",
                  f"  {joins['restarts']} of them called a restart; in "
                  f"{joins['one_mark']} joins the shorter part is one mark, "
                  f"which is never called one"]
    if sheet_flags is not None:
        ruling = (" — for the author's eye, nothing is changed"
                  if sheet_flags else "")
        lines += ["", f"  gold lines the other pages' order flags: "
                      f"{len(sheet_flags)}{ruling}"]
        lines += [f"    {row.get('page', '')} {row.get('district', '')} "
                  f"{row.get('muni_seq', '')},{row.get('settlement_seq', '')}  "
                  f"{row['verdict']}: {row['marks']}   in: {row['sequence']}"
                  for row in sheet_flags]
    if not scores:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["", "  no pass with stored records to judge"])
    lines += ["", f"  each pass, order learned leaving the judged page out, a "
                  f"pair counted from {ORDER_MIN_SEEN} sightings — "
                  f"{scores[0]['level']} level", "",
              f"  {'':26s} {'— scored gold —':^26s}   "
              f"{'— other pages —':^26s}",
              f"  {'pass':26s} {'false':>5s} {'flagged':>7s} {'true':>5s} "
              f"{'flagged':>7s}   {'flagged':>7s} {'on sheet':>8s} "
              f"{'absent':>6s} {'restarts':>9s}"]
    for row in scores:
        lines.append(f"  {row['pass']:26s} {row['false']:5d} "
                     f"{row['false_flagged']:7d} {row['true']:5d} "
                     f"{row['true_flagged']:7d}   {row['flagged_elsewhere']:7d} "
                     f"{row['elsewhere_on_sheets']:8d} "
                     f"{row['elsewhere_absent']:6d} {row['restart_parts']:9d}")
    lines += ["", "  false / true = the pass's claims the reference does not / "
                  "does have; flagged = of those,",
              "  the ones a mark out of place carries. other pages = flagged "
              "claims outside the scored",
              "  gold; on sheet = of those, on a part a calibration sheet "
              "transcribes; absent = the",
              "  sheet does not print that mark there (single-coded sheets, "
              "some still drafts: weaker",
              "  evidence than the scored columns). restarts = parts, on any "
              "page, where the order",
              "  begins again: a boundary to check, not a symbol. The check "
              "flags and routes; no claim",
              "  is changed by it.",
              "  It cannot see a mark misread as another of the same slot "
              "(station / stop,",
              "  revenue office / customs, a savings bank before the "
              "cooperative), nor a missing mark."]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def lexikon_1910_order_disputes_report(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`order_disputes`, one line per pair of readers.

    ``rows`` may be single pairs of passes or means over the repeats of two
    readers; the columns are the same and are printed to one decimal.
    """
    rows = [row for row in rows if row.get("disputed")]
    if not rows:
        return "  no pair of passes with stored records to compare"
    lines = [f"  the order check on disputed claims — {rows[0]['level']} level, "
             f"against {rows[0]['reference']}", "",
             f"  {'first':22s} {'second':22s} {'disputed':>8s} {'false':>6s} "
             f"{'flagged':>7s} {'right':>6s} {'wrong':>6s} {'on 1st':>7s} "
             f"{'on 2nd':>7s}   {'agreed false':>12s} {'flagged':>7s}"]
    for row in rows:
        lines.append(f"  {row['first']:22s} {row['second']:22s} "
                     f"{row['disputed']:8.1f} {row['disputed_false']:6.1f} "
                     f"{row['flagged']:7.1f} {row['flagged_false']:6.1f} "
                     f"{row['flagged_true']:6.1f} {row['first_flagged']:7.1f} "
                     f"{row['second_flagged']:7.1f}   {row['agreed_false']:12.1f} "
                     f"{row['agreed_false_flagged']:7.1f}")
    lines += ["", "  disputed = claims only one of the two makes; false = of "
                  "those, not in the reference.",
              "  flagged = disputed claims whose maker's mark is out of place; "
              "right = the claim is",
              "  indeed false; wrong = it is true; on 1st / on 2nd = whose "
              "claim the flag is on.",
              "  A flag says which reading to look at first, and settles "
              "nothing by itself.",
              "  agreed false = false claims both make, which the pair accepts "
              "unseen; flagged = of",
              "  those, the ones a mark out of place carries in either "
              "reading."]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def compare_passes(passes: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
    """Per-marker agreement across two or more symbol passes.

    ``passes`` maps a label (``"qwen"``, ``"gemma"``) to that run's
